131:             MissingFXRateError: no direct, inverse or cross rate exists, or an
132:                 inverse/cross leg would require dividing by a zero rate.
133:             AmbiguousFXRateError: the source records two distinct rates for
134:                 the same ordered pair and type.
135:         """
136:         base = base_currency.strip().upper()
137:         quote = quote_currency.strip().upper()
138:         rtype = FXRateType(rate_type.value if isinstance(rate_type, FXRateType) else str(rate_type).lower())
139: 
140:         if base == quote:
141:             return ResolvedRate(
142:                 base_currency=base,
143:                 quote_currency=quote,
144:                 rate_type=rtype,
145:                 rate=_ONE,
146:                 method="identity",
147:             )
148: 
149:         # 1. Direct.
150:         direct = self._single(base, quote, rtype)
151:         if direct is not None:
152:             return ResolvedRate(
153:                 base_currency=base,
154:                 quote_currency=quote,
155:                 rate_type=rtype,
156:                 rate=direct.rate,
157:                 method="direct",
158:                 legs=(direct,),
159:             )
160: 
161:         # 2. Inverse (1 / reverse rate).
162:         inverse = self._single(quote, base, rtype)
163:         if inverse is not None:
164:             if inverse.rate == 0:
165:                 raise MissingFXRateError(
166:                     f"cannot invert a zero {rtype.value} rate for {quote}/{base}",
167:                     details={
168:                         "base_currency": base,
169:                         "quote_currency": quote,
170:                         "rate_type": rtype.value,
171:                         "reason": "zero_rate_inverse",
172:                         "source_row": inverse.source_row,
173:                     },
174:                 )
175:             return ResolvedRate(
176:                 base_currency=base,
177:                 quote_currency=quote,
178:                 rate_type=rtype,
179:                 rate=_ONE / inverse.rate,
180:                 method="inverse",
181:                 legs=(inverse,),
182:             )
183: 
184:         # 3. Cross-rate via a shared intermediate currency.
185:         for via in self._cross_candidates(base, quote):
186:             first = self._try_convert(base, via, rtype)
187:             second = self._try_convert(via, quote, rtype)
188:             if first is not None and second is not None:
189:                 return ResolvedRate(
190:                     base_currency=base,
191:                     quote_currency=quote,
192:                     rate_type=rtype,
193:                     rate=first.rate * second.rate,
194:                     method="cross",
195:                     legs=first.legs + second.legs,
196:                     via=via,
197:                 )
198: 
199:         raise MissingFXRateError(
200:             f"no {rtype.value} rate to convert {base} to {quote}",
201:             details={
202:                 "base_currency": base,
203:                 "quote_currency": quote,
204:                 "rate_type": rtype.value,
205:                 "recorded_pairs": sorted(
206:                     f"{r.base_currency}/{r.quote_currency}" for r in self.rates
207:                 ),
208:             },
209:         )
210: 
211:     def _cross_candidates(self, base: str, quote: str) -> list[str]:
212:         """Currencies that appear on both ends of either requested currency."""
213:         connected: set[str] = set()
214:         for rate in self.rates:
215:             for currency in (rate.base_currency, rate.quote_currency):
216:                 if currency not in (base, quote):
217:                     connected.add(currency)
218:         return sorted(connected)
219: 
220:     def _try_convert(
221:         self, base: str, quote: str, rate_type: FXRateType
222:     ) -> ResolvedRate | None:
223:         """Direct-or-inverse resolution for one leg; ``None`` when absent."""
224:         if base == quote:
225:             return ResolvedRate(base, quote, rate_type, _ONE, "identity")
226:         direct = self._single(base, quote, rate_type)
227:         if direct is not None:
228:             return ResolvedRate(base, quote, rate_type, direct.rate, "direct", (direct,))
229:         inverse = self._single(quote, base, rate_type)
230:         if inverse is not None and inverse.rate != 0:
231:             return ResolvedRate(
232:                 base, quote, rate_type, _ONE / inverse.rate, "inverse", (inverse,)
233:             )
234:         return None
235: 
236:     # -- convenience -------------------------------------------------------
237: 
238:     def convert(
239:         self,
240:         amount: Decimal,
241:         base_currency: str,
242:         quote_currency: str,
243:         rate_type: FXRateType | str,
244:     ) -> Decimal:
245:         """Convert ``amount`` at the resolved rate, at full precision.
246: 
247:         No rounding is applied here — the policy rounds only reported figures
248:         (``models.round_reported``).
249:         """
250:         resolved = self.resolve(base_currency, quote_currency, rate_type)
251:         return amount * resolved.rate

25: _SENSITIVE_VALUE_RES = [
26:     re.compile(r"AIza[0-9A-Za-z_\-]{35}"),  # Google API key
27:     re.compile(r"sk-[0-9A-Za-z_\-]{16,}"),  # generic secret key
28: ]
29: 
30: _MASK = "***REDACTED***"
31: 
32: 
33: def redact(value: Any, extra_secrets: Iterable[str] = ()) -> Any:
34:     """Recursively mask secrets in strings, dicts and lists."""
35:     secrets = [s for s in extra_secrets if s and len(s) >= 8]
36: 
37:     if isinstance(value, str):
38:         out = value
39:         for secret in secrets:
40:             if secret in out:
41:                 out = out.replace(secret, _MASK)
42:         for pattern in _SENSITIVE_VALUE_RES:
43:             out = pattern.sub(_MASK, out)
44:         return out
45:     if isinstance(value, dict):
46:         redacted: dict[Any, Any] = {}
47:         for key, item in value.items():
48:             if isinstance(key, str) and _SENSITIVE_KEY_RE.search(key):
49:                 redacted[key] = _MASK
50:             else:
51:                 redacted[key] = redact(item, secrets)
52:         return redacted
53:     if isinstance(value, list):
54:         return [redact(item, secrets) for item in value]
55:     if isinstance(value, tuple):
56:         return tuple(redact(item, secrets) for item in value)
57:     return value
58: 
59: 
60: def _now() -> str:
61:     return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
62: 
63: 
64: class TraceRecorder:
65:     """Append-only JSONL recorder bound to a single execution trace."""
66: 
67:     def __init__(self, traces_dir: str | Path, trace_id: str) -> None:
68:         self.trace_id = trace_id
69:         self.path = Path(traces_dir) / f"{trace_id}.jsonl"
70:         # Resume numbering so a recorder rebuilt for the same trace (one is
71:         # created per graph node) continues the file instead of restarting.
72:         self._seq = 0
73:         if self.path.is_file():
74:             try:
75:                 with self.path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
76:                     self._seq = sum(1 for line in handle if line.strip())
77:             except OSError:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
78:                 self._seq = 0
79: 
80:     def event(
81:         self,
82:         event: str,
83:         payload: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
84:         *,
85:         secrets: Iterable[str] = (),
86:     ) -> dict[str, Any]:
87:         """Append one event; returns the record that was written."""
88:         self._seq += 1
89:         record = {
90:             "ts": _now(),
91:             "seq": self._seq,
92:             "trace_id": self.trace_id,
93:             "event": event,
94:             "payload": redact(payload or {}, secrets),
95:         }
96:         append_jsonl(self.path, record)
97:         return record
98: 
99:     def read_events(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
100:         """Read back every event recorded for this trace."""
101:         if not self.path.is_file():
102:             return []
103:         return list(iter_jsonl(self.path))
```

## Design (Phase 1 → 2)

**Key decisions from inspection:**
- Skill name: `consolidation` (matches `consolidation_intent(...).kind == "consolidation"` so `select_by_intent` selects it with no hint).
- Mode: `CONSOLIDATION` only.
- Tool policy: `READ_ONLY` (defence-in-depth; all MCP tools are read-only). Permitted tools: `list_entities`, `get_trial_balance`, `get_group_coa`, `get_account_mapping`, `get_fx_rates`.
- **No intercompany reconciliation service exists** (only the raw `get_intercompany` reader) → that stage is `blocked`. No FX-translation/elimination/goodwill/NCI/translation-reserve/statement services exist → all `pending`/`blocked`.
- The skill calls the deterministic services (`TrialBalanceIngestor`, `TrialBalanceValidator`, `AccountMapper`, `FXService`) which consume the **same** source data the skill retrieves via MCP — no source reader duplicated, source retrieval gated by the gateway.

  "content": "\"\"\"Consolidation readiness models (Consolidation Skill v1).\n\nThe accounting engine is deliberately incomplete: only ingestion, validation,\nFX-rate resolution and account mapping are implemented. This module records,\ndeterministically, **which** consolidation stages have actually run and which\nare blocked/pending, so a skill can never claim a consolidation is complete\nwhen a required stage has not executed.\n\nNothing here performs financial arithmetic. The readiness model only carries\nthe typed outputs of the Stage 1/2 services plus a per-stage status ledger.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom enum import Enum\nfrom typing import Any\n\nfrom pydantic import BaseModel, Field\n\nfrom app.accounting.models import (\n    MappedTrialBalance,\n    Severity,\n    ValidationIssue,\n    ValidationResult,\n)\n\n\nclass StageStatus(str, Enum):\n    \"\"\"Whether one consolidation stage actually executed.\"\"\"\n\n    COMPLETED = \"completed\"   # ran successfully on the real services\n    BLOCKED = \"blocked\"       # a required dependency is missing / not built\n    PENDING = \"pending\"       # not attempted yet in this increment\n    FAILED = \"failed\"         # attempted and raised / produced an error\n\n\nclass StageOutcome(BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"The recorded outcome of one consolidation stage.\"\"\"\n\n    model_config = {\"frozen\": True}\n\n    stage: str\n    status: StageStatus\n    detail: str = \"\"\n    # True when the stage is mandatory before a consolidation can be *called*\n    # complete. Ingestion/validation/mapping are candidates; translation and\n    # beyond are required too, but not yet implemented.\n    required_for_complete: bool = True\n\n\n# The full stage ledger, in execution order. ``implemented`` reflects the\n# actual repository state at consolidation-skill v1; it is data, not a claim.\nSTAGE_ORDER: tuple[tuple[str, bool, bool], ...] = (\n    # (stage, implemented, required_for_complete)\n    (\"trial_balance_ingestion\", True, True),\n    (\"trial_balance_validation\", True, True),\n    (\"account_mapping\", True, True),\n    (\"intercompany_reconciliation\", False, True),\n    (\"fx_translation\", False, True),\n    (\"intercompany_elimination\", False, True),\n    (\"goodwill\", False, False),\n    (\"nci\", False, False),\n    (\"translation_reserve\", False, True),\n    (\"financial_statement_assembly\", False, True),\n)\n\n# Stages whose absence means the run cannot even reach a *validated, mapped*\n# position (the minimum this increment can guarantee).\n_BLOCKING_MISSING = {\n    \"intercompany_reconciliation\",\n    \"fx_translation\",\n    \"intercompany_elimination\",\n    \"translation_reserve\",\n    \"financial_statement_assembly\",\n}\n\n\nclass EntityConsolidationResult(BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"Per-entity outputs of ingestion, validation and mapping.\"\"\"\n\n    entity: str\n    functional_currency: str\n    source_file: str | None = None\n    row_count: int = 0\n    balanced: bool = False\n    # Full-precision functional-currency totals (never rounded here).\n    debit_total: str = \"0\"\n    credit_total: str = \"0\"\n    difference: str = \"0\"\n    mapped_row_count: int = 0\n    unmapped_row_count: int = 0\n    issues: list[ValidationIssue] = Field(default_factory=list)\n\n    @property\n    def error_count(self) -> int:\n        return sum(1 for i in self.issues if i.severity is Severity.ERROR)\n\n    @property\n    def warning_count(self) -> int:\n        return sum(1 for i in self.issues if i.severity is Severity.WARNING)\n\n\nclass ConsolidationReadiness(BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"Typed consolidation-readiness result returned by the skill.\n\n    This is **not** a set of consolidated statements. It records what actually\n    ran, what is missing, and the validated/mapped per-entity position. The\n    ``complete`` flag is only ever True when every required stage is\n    ``COMPLETED`` — which cannot happen in v1.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    period: str\n    scope: str = \"group\"\n    entities: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)\n    functional_currency: str = \"GBP\"\n\n    stages: list[StageOutcome] = Field(default_factory=list)\n    entity_results: dict[str, EntityConsolidationResult] = Field(\n        default_factory=dict\n    )\n    issues: list[ValidationIssue] = Field(default_factory=list)\n\n    # Deterministic summary flags (no figures are fabricated to fill gaps).\n    complete: bool = False\n\n    # --- derived views --------------------------------------------------\n\n    @property\n    def blocked_stages(self) -> list[str]:\n        return [\n            s.stage\n            for s in self.stages\n            if s.status in (StageStatus.BLOCKED, StageStatus.FAILED)\n        ]\n\n    @property\n    def pending_stages(self) -> list[str]:\n        return [s.stage for s in self.stages if s.status is StageStatus.PENDING]\n\n    @property\n    def completed_stages(self) -> list[str]:\n        return [\n            s.stage for s in self.stages if s.status is StageStatus.COMPLETED\n        ]\n\n    @property\n    def missing_required_stages(self) -> list[str]:\n        \"\"\"Required stages that are not ``COMPLETED``.\"\"\"\n        return [\n            s.stage\n            for s in self.stages\n            if s.required_for_complete and s.status is not StageStatus.COMPLETED\n        ]\n\n    def to_payload(self) -> dict[str, Any]:\n        \"\"\"A serialisable view for ``SkillResult.data`` / traces.\n\n        Decimal totals are stringified (full precision preserved), and\n        issues are expanded to plain dicts. No accounting figure is invented:\n        every value here was produced by an executed stage.\n        \"\"\"\n        return {\n            \"period\": self.period,\n            \"scope\": self.scope,\n            \"entities\": list(self.entities),\n            \"functional_currency\": self.functional_currency,\n            \"complete\": self.complete,\n            \"stages\": [\n                {\n                    \"stage\": s.stage,\n                    \"status\": s.status.value,\n                    \"detail\": s.detail,\n                    \"required_for_complete\": s.required_for_complete,\n                }\n                for s in self.stages\n            ],\n            \"completed_stages\": self.completed_stages,\n            \"blocked_stages\": self.blocked_stages,\n            \"pending_stages\": self.pending_stages,\n            \"missing_required_stages\": self.missing_required_stages,\n            \"entities_detail\": {\n                name: {\n                    \"functional_currency\": r.functional_currency,\n                    \"source_file\": r.source_file,\n                    \"row_count\": r.row_count,\n                    \"balanced\": r.balanced,\n                    \"debit_total\": r.debit_total,\n                    \"credit_total\": r.credit_total,\n                    \"difference\": r.difference,\n                    \"mapped_row_count\": r.mapped_row_count,\n                    \"unmapped_row_count\": r.unmapped_row_count,\n                    \"error_count\": r.error_count,\n                    \"warning_count\": r.warning_count,\n                }\n                for name, r in self.entity_results.items()\n            },\n        }\n\n\ndef build_stage_ledger(\n    *,\n    ingestion: bool,\n    validation: bool,\n    mapping: bool,\n) -> list[StageOutcome]:\n    \"\"\"Compose the stage ledger from what actually executed.\n\n    Any stage not marked implemented in :data:`STAGE_ORDER` is reported\n    ``BLOCKED`` (missing dependency) rather than silently skipped, so the\n    caller can always see the unimplemented remainder explicitly.\n    \"\"\"\n    executed = {\n        \"trial_balance_ingestion\": ingestion,\n        \"trial_balance_validation\": validation,\n        \"account_mapping\": mapping,\n    }\n    ledger: list[StageOutcome] = []\n    for stage, implemented, required in STAGE_ORDER:\n        if not implemented:\n            ledger.append(\n                StageOutcome(\n                    stage=stage,\n                    status=StageStatus.BLOCKED,\n                    detail=\"service not implemented in consolidation-skill v1\",\n                    required_for_complete=required,\n                )\n            )\n        elif executed.get(stage):\n            ledger.append(\n                StageOutcome(\n                    stage=stage,\n                    status=StageStatus.COMPLETED,\n                    detail=\"executed\",\n                    required_for_complete=required,\n                )\n            )\n        else:\n            ledger.append(\n                StageOutcome(\n                    stage=stage,\n                    status=StageStatus.FAILED,\n                    detail=\"stage did not complete\",\n                    required_for_complete=required,\n                )\n            )\n    return ledger\n"
}

The skill's `execute` will:
1. Validate period (FY2024 required).
2. `list_entities` via MCP → determine entities.
3. `get_trial_balance` per entity via MCP (source retrieval gated by gateway).
4. Ingest via `TrialBalanceIngestor`, validate via `TrialBalanceValidator`, map via `AccountMapper`.
5. FX readiness checks via `FXService`.
6. Build stage ledger + readiness result.
7. Return `SkillResult` (BLOCKED, since required stages are missing).

It must NOT call `SourceDataService` directly for source retrieval — but the deterministic services need source data. The instruction says: *"Deterministic accounting services may consume the retrieved source data or use their existing SourceDataService dependency as appropriate. Do not duplicate source readers."* So the services use their own `SourceDataService`, while the skill's MCP calls (via gateway) are the traced source-retrieval path. I'll have the skill call MCP for the entities/trial balances it *reports*, and use the services (with the same underlying data dir) for computation. To keep the MCP calls meaningful and traced, the skill uses the MCP-returned entity list and per-entity TB presence to drive the loop.

# Consolidation Skill v1 — Deliverable Report

## A. Skill architecture and execution flow

The skill plugs into the **existing** shared LangGraph agent with no architectural change. Flow:

```
AgentRunner.run(mode="consolidation", payload={"period":"2024",...})
  └─ graph: load_context → identify_intent (deterministic) → select_skill
              → execute_skill → finalize
                 └─ registry.get("consolidation") → gateway.bind(skill.spec, mode, trace)
                    └─ ConsolidationSkill.execute(SkillContext)
                       1. validate period / scope           (no tools)
                       2. list_entities          (MCP, traced)
                       3. get_trial_balance ×N   (MCP, traced)
                       4. TrialBalanceIngestor   (deterministic service)
                       5. TrialBalanceValidator  (deterministic service)
                       6. AccountMapper          (deterministic service)
                       7. get_fx_rates (MCP) + FXService.resolve  (readiness)
                       8. build stage ledger → ConsolidationReadiness
                    → SkillResult(status=BLOCKED, data=readiness, issues=…)
```

The skill never computes a figure itself: every number comes from `TrialBalanceIngestor` / `TrialBalanceValidator` / `AccountMapper` / `FXService`. The LLM (absent here) only orchestrates; consolidation intent is derived deterministically in `graph.consolidation_intent`, so the whole run works with no `GEMINI_API_KEY`.

## B. Files created and modified

**Created**
- `backend/app/agents/skills/consolidation.py` — the `ConsolidationSkill`.
- `backend/app/accounting/consolidation.py` — stage ledger + readiness models (`StageStatus`, `StageOutcome`, `EntityConsolidationResult`, `ConsolidationReadiness`, `build_stage_ledger`).
- `backend/tests/test_consolidation_skill.py` — 31 tests.

**Modified**
- `backend/app/agents/skills/registry.py` — `build_default_registry()` now registers `ConsolidationSkill()`.
- `backend/tests/test_skill_registry.py` — replaced the now-obsolete `test_default_registry_is_empty_until_milestone4` with a check that the real skill is registered and mode-limited.

Untouched: `data/northwind/` (`git diff -- data/` empty), frontend, API, MCP server/client, gateway, graph, runner, base skill contract, StateGraph. No commits or staging.

## C. How the skill is registered and selected

- Registered in `build_default_registry()` → `SkillRegistry([ConsolidationSkill()])`.
- Spec name is `consolidation`, which equals the deterministic intent `kind` from `graph.consolidation_intent`, so `select_by_intent("consolidation", CONSOLIDATION)` picks it with **no LLM hint**. An explicit `payload["skill"]="consolidation"` hint also resolves it.
- Mode permission is explicit: `allowed_modes={AgentMode.CONSOLIDATION}`. `registry.resolve("consolidation", COPILOT)` raises `SkillNotAllowedForModeError` (tested).
- I did **not** touch the Financial Analysis stub (`StubAnalysisSkill`) or the existing fixtures; the `financial_analysis` copilot skill remains a later milestone.

## D. MCP tools used and their permissions

Policy: `ToolPolicy.READ_ONLY` (fail-closed; all five tools carry `read_only_hint=True` on the server). Permitted tools:

| Tool | Use |
|---|---|
| `list_entities` | discover US/UK/IN and their currencies |
| `get_trial_balance` | retrieve each entity's raw TB (traced) |
| `get_fx_rates` | pull the rate table for the FX readiness check |
| `get_group_coa` | declared (account context) |
| `get_account_mapping` | declared (mapping context) |

All retrieval goes through `context.tool_gateway.call(...)`; any tool outside `permitted_tools` is rejected with `ToolPolicyError(reason="not_permitted")`, and the per-execution budget (`AGENT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS`, default 25) is enforced (both tested). Gateway calls are recorded and traced automatically (the skill does **not** re-add them). The accounting services consume the same immutable source through their existing `SourceDataService` dependency — no reader was duplicated.

## E. Actual accounting stages executed

- **trial_balance_ingestion** — completed for US, UK, IN.
- **trial_balance_validation** — completed; all three balance (US debit `43534373.43`, UK credit `15688717.72`, IN debit `1805000000.00`, matching Stage 1).
- **account_mapping** — completed; 25/23/20 rows mapped, 0 unmapped.
- **FX readiness** (via `FXService.resolve`, not a full translation stage) — all required FY2024 rates resolve: USD→GBP closing/average, INR→GBP closing/h2_average.

## F. Remaining blocked stages

Reported `BLOCKED` because no service exists (no fabrication): `intercompany_reconciliation` (only a raw `get_intercompany` reader exists, no reconciliation logic), `fx_translation`, `intercompany_elimination`, `goodwill`, `nci`, `translation_reserve`, `financial_statement_assembly`.

Required-for-complete missing stages: `intercompany_reconciliation`, `fx_translation`, `intercompany_elimination`, `translation_reserve`, `financial_statement_assembly` → so **`complete` is always False and status is `BLOCKED`** in v1.

(The single warning is the known UK 2310 Deferred income → 4100 mapping concern, surfaced unchanged from Stage 2.)

## H. Test results

- Full backend suite: **177 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** (was 146; **+31 new**).
- New skill tests cover all 15 required areas: registration; selection; copilot-mode rejection; invalid/missing period; MCP retrieval via gateway; permission + budget enforcement; ingestion for all three entities; validation; mapping; issue propagation; blocked/pending stage handling; no fabricated statements; missing Gemini key; complete execution trace; end-to-end AgentRunner → graph → skill → MCP → service.
- `compileall app tests`: clean. `pyflakes` on the new modules/tests: clean.
- No live LLM calls (consolidation mode is deterministic; an unconfigured LLM is asserted in-test).

## I. Known limitations

- v1 is a **readiness** run: it stops before translation/elimination/statements by design. `complete` can never be True until those services exist.
- Intercompany reconciliation is `BLOCKED` (no tested implementation) rather than attempted on the raw reader.
- FX is a *readiness* check only (rates resolve) — no entity balances are translated.
- The `get_group_coa` / `get_account_mapping` tools are permitted and available but not currently called by the skill (mapping/COA work is delegated to `AccountMapper`, which reads the same source); they’re declared for the documented account-context step.
- In production the skill’s services and the MCP server must share the same `DATA_DIR`; tests bind both explicitly.

## J. Recommended next milestone

**Intercompany reconciliation service** — it is the next real, tested accounting stage (the raw `intercompany.csv` already exists and group accounts 2150/1250/4200/6300 give verifiable cases), it unblocks a required stage in the ledger, and it is the natural prerequisite for FX translation + intercompany elimination. Build it as a deterministic service (like Stage 1/2), then extend `ConsolidationSkill` to execute it and move `intercompany_reconciliation` from `BLOCKED` to `COMPLETED`.

**Stop condition respected:** only Consolidation Skill v1 was implemented; no eliminations, goodwill, NCI, translation reserve, statement assembly, Financial Analysis skill, API endpoints or frontend work. The run never claims final consolidation is complete.

111:         hint that does not serve this mode raises
112:         ``SkillNotAllowedForModeError``. Without a hint we match the intent
113:         kind, then fall back to the single mode-allowed skill when there is

122:                 )

144:                 "output_expectations": list(s.spec.output_expectations),
145:             }
146:             for s in skills
147:         ]

Reject anything else before touching the data.\n2. **Load entity context.** Call `list_entities` through the MCP tool gateway\n   to discover the group's entities (US, UK, IN) and their currencies.\n3. **Retrieve trial balances.** Call `get_trial_balance` for each selected\n   entity through the MCP tool gateway. Retrieval is read-only and traced.\n4. **Ingest.** Hand each raw trial balance to `TrialBalanceIngestor`, which\n   normalises the US/UK/IN schemas into typed rows.\n5. **Validate.** Run `TrialBalanceValidator` over each ingested trial balance\n   (debit/credit balance, row and schema checks).\n6. **Map accounts.** Resolve local accounts to the group chart with\n   `AccountMapper`, preserving source traceability.\n7. **FX readiness.** Pull `get_fx_rates` via MCP and confirm the required\n   FY2024 policy rates resolve (via `FXService`). This is a readiness check,\n   not a translation.\n8. **Assemble readiness.** Build the stage ledger and return a typed\n   consolidation-readiness result that names every completed and every\n   blocked/pending stage.\n\nStages 1–3 are orchestration; stages 4–8 delegate to existing deterministic\nservices. The skill does not reimplement any accounting logic.\n\n## Required input\n\n- `period`: an explicit supported reporting period (FY2024), supplied in the\n  structured payload and/or intent.\n- `scope`: `group`.\n- Optional `entities`: a subset of the group; when omitted, all known\n  entities are included.\n\n## Expected output\n\nA typed `SkillResult` whose `data` is a consolidation-**readiness** payload:\n\n- per-entity row counts, balance status and mapping counts;\n- a stage ledger with an explicit status per stage\n  (`completed` / `blocked` / `pending` / `failed`);\n- the list of completed, blocked, pending and required-but-missing stages;\n- collected structured issues.\n\nIt is **not** a set of consolidated financial statements and never contains\nfabricated figures. In this increment `complete` is always `false` because\nrequired accounting stages are not yet implemented.\n\n## Accounting and data-integrity rules\n\n- All financial values come from the deterministic services. The agent must\n  never compute, adjust or estimate a financial figure.\n- Full precision is preserved by the services; rounding, if ever required,\n  happens only at the reporting boundary per the group policy.\n- Trial balances are validated, never auto-corrected. An unbalanced trial\n  balance is reported, not silently fixed.\n- Source rows are never dropped, and their traceability is preserved.\n- Many-to-one account mappings are valid aggregation and are not errors.\n- Ambiguous or conflicting mappings are reported, never auto-resolved.\n- Missing FX rates are reported as such; a rate is never invented.\n\n## MCP tool usage rules\n\n- Access source data **only** through the MCP tool gateway\n  (`context.tool_gateway.call(...)`). Never read source files directly and\n  never bypass the gateway.\n- Use only the tools declared in this skill's `ToolPolicy`\n  (`read_only`): `list_entities`, `get_trial_balance`, `get_group_coa`,\n  `get_account_mapping`, `get_fx_rates`.\n- Respect the per-execution tool-call budget; do not attempt to widen it.\n- Every gateway call is recorded and traced automatically; the skill must not\n  re-record gateway calls in its own result.\n- Read-only access only. No tool may mutate source data.\n\n## Handling missing data and unresolved issues\n\n- If a required stage's service does not exist, mark that stage `blocked` and\n  name it in the result — do not fabricate its output.\n- If a trial balance cannot be retrieved or ingested, record a structured\n  error issue and mark the affected stages not completed.\n- If an FX rate cannot be resolved, record a structured warning; never guess\n  a rate.\n- If the reporting period or scope is invalid, reject the request with a\n  typed validation result and make no MCP calls.\n- Never claim the consolidation is complete while any required stage is\n  missing.\n\n## Explicit restrictions\n\n- **Never fabricate financial values.** Every number must come from a\n  deterministic service reading the immutable source data.\n- **Never bypass journal validation.** Year-end adjustments are only posted\n  if valid for FY2024; invalid journals must not be posted.\n- **Never modify original source files.** `data/northwind/` is read-only.\n- **Never perform accounting calculations using the LLM.** The LLM may\n  orchestrate and summarise; all arithmetic is deterministic Python.\n",

## 🤖 Assistant

Everything is in scope. `test_mcp_server.py`/`test_system.py` are from the earlier milestone; `registry.py` was changed in the previous milestone too. My new changes this milestone are `graph.py`, `base.py`, `skill_instructions.py`, the `consolidation/` dir, and the new test file.

## Integration approach (as implemented)

**How SKILL.md integrates with the existing architecture:**

1. **Layout.** The document lives at `backend/app/agents/skills/consolidation/SKILL.md`. The directory contains **only** `SKILL.md` and no `__init__.py`, so Python's module resolution keeps `consolidation.py` as the importable implementation (`import app.agents.skills.consolidation` is unchanged). This is the key trick that avoids moving or renaming any Python code — verified empirically.

2. **Lightweight loader.** `skill_instructions.py` is a ~60-line helper: `skill_instructions_path(name)` → `<skills_root>/<name>/SKILL.md`, plus `load_skill_instructions`, `has_skill_instructions`, and a typed `SkillInstructionsNotFound`. No framework, no registry of loaders.

3. **Association.** `Skill.instructions_doc()` (added to the base contract) lazily resolves and caches the document for **its own** `spec.name`. Skills without a document return `None`. Frozen `SkillSpec` is untouched — the Markdown is supplementary agent-facing guidance, not a replacement for `spec.instructions`.

4. **Availability at selection.** The graph's `select_skill`/`execute_skill` populates `SkillContext.skill_instructions` with **only the selected skill's** document and records `has_instructions` on the `skill_selected` trace event. No other skill's instructions are ever surfaced.

5. **Execution unchanged.** The Python `ConsolidationSkill.execute` still performs all deterministic work and delegates to the same services. MCP permissions, budgets, and tracing are untouched (the gateway/graph paths weren't restructured).

## Changed files

**Created**
- `backend/app/agents/skills/consolidation/SKILL.md` — agent-facing instruction document.
- `backend/app/agents/skills/skill_instructions.py` — lightweight loader.
- `backend/tests/test_skill_instructions.py` — 22 tests.

**Modified**
- `backend/app/agents/skills/base.py` — added `_UNSET` sentinel, `Skill.instructions_doc()`, and `SkillContext.skill_instructions`.
- `backend/app/agents/graph.py` — populate `skill_instructions` for the selected skill; add `has_instructions` to the `skill_selected` trace.

**Untouched:** `data/northwind/` (empty `git diff`), frontend, API, MCP server/client, gateway, runner, `ConsolidationSkill` execution logic, `SkillSpec`. Nothing staged or committed.

## Test results

- Full backend suite: **199 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** (was 177; **+22 new**).
- New tests cover all five required areas: file existence and loading (incl. missing/invalid-name errors and required document sections); Markdown↔Python association (correct doc, per-instance caching, `None` for doc-less skills); instructions exposed **only** for the selected skill; existing deterministic execution still working (BLOCKED readiness, 3 stages, MCP calls through the gateway); permission (`not_permitted`) and budget (`budget_exhausted`) enforcement intact.
- `compileall app tests`: clean. `pyflakes` on the changed modules: clean. No LLM calls; all MCP traffic in-memory.

No new accounting stages, API endpoints, frontend changes, or skills were added.

One note for your awareness: the `consolidation/` directory holding `SKILL.md` currently works because Python prefers the sibling `.py` module in this namespace-package layout. If someone later adds `consolidation/__init__.py` (or any `.py` inside the directory), it would shadow `consolidation.py` — worth keeping in mind, though nothing in the task requires that.

## 👤 User

# Milestone: LedgerFlow API + UI Integration (Readiness Dashboard)

We have completed:
- Core LangGraph agent infrastructure.
- MCP server/client and ToolGateway.
- Skill registry.
- ConsolidationSkill Python implementation.
- Consolidation SKILL.md instruction layer.
- Trial balance ingestion, validation and account mapping.
- Consolidation readiness result.

Now make the existing Consolidation Skill executable from the existing Next.js frontend.

## Phase 1 — Inspect before implementation

Inspect:
- Existing FastAPI application and router structure.
- AgentRunner and its execution result types.
- ConsolidationSkill and ConsolidationReadiness models.
- Thread and trace persistence.
- Existing frontend pages, components and design system.

Reuse existing architecture. Do not create duplicate agent runners, registries, services or persistence systems.

## Phase 2 — Backend API

Implement a minimal API for consolidation execution.

Required capabilities:

1. Start a FY2024 consolidation run.
2. Return a unique execution/run ID.
3. Return the actual AgentRunner execution result.
4. Expose the structured ConsolidationReadiness result.
5. Expose execution traces and MCP tool calls.
6. Expose the issues and blocked stages.

Use appropriate request/response Pydantic models.

Suggested API structure (adapt to existing conventions):

- POST /api/consolidations/runs
- GET /api/consolidations/runs/{run_id}
- GET /api/consolidations/runs/{run_id}/trace

Important:
- Use the existing AgentRunner and build_default_registry().
- Do not bypass LangGraph or call ConsolidationSkill directly from the API.
- Do not fabricate results.
- Preserve execution errors and typed failure responses.
- Do not expose secrets or API keys in traces.
- Make sure the application works without PostgreSQL and without GEMINI_API_KEY.
- Do not introduce unnecessary background-task infrastructure. Choose the simplest reliable execution model compatible with the existing architecture.
- If execution is synchronous initially, make the UI loading state clear.

## Phase 3 — Frontend

Use the existing Next.js frontend and its existing design system.

Build a professional financial consolidation dashboard with:

### A. Header
- LedgerFlow branding.
- Reporting period: FY2024.
- Presentation currency: GBP.
- Consolidation run status.

### B. Entity overview
Show:
- Northwind Inc. — USD.
- Northwind UK Ltd — GBP.
- Northwind India Pvt Ltd — INR.

Display actual validation and mapping statuses from the backend.

### C. Consolidation execution
- Run Consolidation button.
- Loading state while the backend executes.
- Disable duplicate execution while a run is in progress.
- Display run ID and execution status.

### D. Results
Display actual backend results:
- Trial balance ingestion.
- Trial balance validation.
- Account mapping.
- Intercompany reconciliation.
- FX translation.
- Eliminations.
- Goodwill.
- NCI.
- Translation reserve.
- Financial statement assembly.

Use clear completed, blocked, pending and failed statuses.

### E. Issues panel
Show:
- Issue severity.
- Issue code.
- Description.
- Source file/row where available.
- Affected amount where available.
- Treatment.

### F. Agent activity
Show actual execution trace events and MCP tool calls, including their status and duration when available.

## Phase 4 — Testing

Backend:
- API tests for successful run.
- API tests for invalid request.
- API tests for execution errors.
- Verify real AgentRunner → LangGraph → ConsolidationSkill execution.
- Verify traces and issue propagation.
- Verify no Gemini key is required.
- Verify PostgreSQL can remain stopped.

Frontend:
- Run button calls the actual backend.
- Loading and error states work.
- Results are rendered from API responses, not hardcoded accounting values.
- Refreshing a run view retrieves the actual persisted run if persistence is supported.

## Strict boundaries

- Do not implement new accounting calculations.
- Do not implement intercompany reconciliation yet.
- Do not implement FX translation or eliminations.
- Do not implement Financial Analysis Skill or Copilot chat.
- Do not use mock data as the actual dashboard result.
- Do not modify data/northwind/.
- Do not modify unrelated architecture.
- Do not stage or commit changes.

At completion, report:
1. API endpoints implemented.
2. Frontend pages/components created or modified.
3. Actual execution flow.
4. Persistence behavior.
5. Tests and results.
6. Exact

3: Phase 1 persists everything on the filesystem. This module centralises

67:         return self.data_dir

70:         """Create writable directories if they do not exist.
71: 
72:         The source data directory is never created or modified here; it is
73:         treated as immutable input.

79:             self.agent_logs_dir,

90: # --- persistence primitives -------------------------------------------------
91: 
92: 
93: def atomic_write_json(path: str | Path, data: Any) -> None:
94:     """Write JSON atomically (temp file in the same dir + ``os.replace``)."""
95:     target = Path(path)
96:     try:
97:         target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
98:         fd, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(
99:             prefix=f".{target.name}.", suffix=".tmp", dir=str(target.parent)
100:         )
101:         try:
102:             with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
103:                 json.dump(data, handle, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2, default=str)
104:                 handle.flush()
105:                 os.fsync(handle.fileno())
106:             os.replace(tmp_name, target)
107:         finally:
108:             if os.path.exists(tmp_name):
109:                 os.unlink(tmp_name)
110:     except OSError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
111:         raise StorageError(f"failed to write {target}", details={"path": str(target)}) from exc
112: 
113: 
114: def read_json(path: str | Path) -> Any:
115:     """Read a JSON file. Raises ``StorageError`` when it does not exist."""
116:     target = Path(path)
117:     if not target.is_file():
118:         raise StorageError(f"missing json file: {target}", details={"path": str(target)})
119:     try:
120:         with target.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
121:             return json.load(handle)
122:     except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
123:         raise StorageError(
124:             f"unreadable json file: {target}", details={"path": str(target)}
125:         ) from exc
126: 
127: 
128: def append_jsonl(path: str | Path, record: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
129:     """Append one JSON record as a line (used for execution traces)."""
130:     target = Path(path)
131:     try:
132:         target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
133:         with target.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
134:             handle.write(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False, default=str) + "\n")
135:     except OSError as exc:
136:         raise StorageError(
137:             f"failed to append to {target}", details={"path": str(target)}
138:         ) from exc
139: 
140: 
141: def iter_jsonl(path: str | Path) -> Iterator[dict[str, Any]]:
142:     """Yield records from a JSONL file, skipping malformed lines."""
143:     target = Path(path)
144:     if not target.is_file():
145:         raise StorageError(f"missing jsonl file: {target}", details={"path": str(target)})
146:     with target.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
147:         for line in handle:
148:             line = line.strip()
149:             if not line:
150:                 continue
151:             try:
152:                 yield json.loads(line)
153:             except json.JSONDecodeError:
154:                 continue

12: 
13: Many apps can provide responsive interactions without a client data-fetching library. If a Client Component only needs to read server data once, [pass it a Promise and unwrap it with React's `use()`](/docs/app/getting-started/fetching-data#streaming-data-with-the-use-api).
14: 
15: This avoids adding a library for data that never revalidates on the client. See [Building interactive apps](/docs/app/guides/interactive-apps) for patterns using Server Functions, transitions, optimistic UI, and pending feedback.
16: 
17: Use a client data-fetching library such as [SWR](https://swr.vercel.app), [TanStack Query](https://tanstack.com/query), or [Apollo Client](https://www.apollographql.com/docs/react) when Client Components need a shared browser cache. These libraries can add focus revalidation, interval polling, request deduplication, or optimistic updates across components.
18: 
19: ## Choose a client fetching pattern
20: 
21: First decide whether the initial view needs data from the server or can wait for a browser request after hydration. Client data-fetching libraries support three common patterns:
22: 
23: | Pattern                 | SWR                            | TanStack Query        | When data becomes available            |
24: | ----------------------- | ------------------------------ | --------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
25: | Inline loading states   | `useSWR`                       | `useQuery`            | Browser request after hydration        |
26: | Suspense loading states | `useSWR` with `suspense: true` | `useSuspenseQuery`    | Browser request after hydration        |
27: | Provided by the server  | `<SWRConfig fallback>`         | `<HydrationBoundary>` | Initial render or streamed from server |
28: 
29: Use inline loading states when each component should render its own loading UI. Use [Suspense](/docs/app/getting-started/fetching-data#streaming) to define loading UI at a boundary and coordinate which parts of the interface reveal together or progressively. For client-only fetching, choose the pattern that matches the loading experience you want. Suspense coordinates rendering, while the data library and component structure determine when requests start.
30: 
31: For browser-driven interactions such as autocomplete, you can use either client-only pattern. The initial result waits for hydration and a browser request, which is often the right tradeoff for data that is not needed until an interaction.
32: 
33: Provide initial data from a [Server Component](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components) when the server knows what the initial render needs. The value can be included in the initial render or streamed through Suspense. The library receives it in the React Server Component payload and can continue managing it in the browser.
34: 
35: ## Cache server data with Cache Components (optional)
36: 
37: Providing initial data and caching it on the server are independent choices. Add Cache Components when the server read or rendered view should be reused. When both are enabled, three cache layers can hold related data:
38: 
39: | Layer                        | What it stores                                                    | Freshness control                                                                    |
40: | ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
41: | Next.js server cache         | Cached data and Server Component output                           | [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) `revalidate` and `expire` |
42: | Next.js client cache         | React Server Component payloads for visited and prefetched routes | [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) `stale`                   |
43: | Client data-fetching library | Browser data stored under an SWR key or TanStack query key        | The library's revalidation options and mutations                                     |
44: 
45: Next.js [prefetching](/docs/app/guides/prefetching) can place a route's React Server Component payload in the client cache before navigation.
46: 
47: The cache layers keep independent freshness policies and do not need matching durations. Cache identities and mutation invalidation must stay coordinated across layers.
48: 
49: ## Coordinate mutations
50: 
51: Server Components, data-fetching libraries, and mutations manage different parts of the data flow:
52: 
53: - **Server Components** provide the initial data, scoped to the segment that owns it.
54: - **The data-fetching library** stores the browser value under a shared cache identity.
55: - **Mutations** can update the browser cache immediately and invalidate cached server data so the next render can read a fresh value.
56: 
57: An optimistic update should restore the previous browser value if the write fails. If the server read is not cached, there is no server tag to invalidate.
58: 
59: After a mutation, invalidate any cached server read that provided the initial data:
60: 
61: | Method                                                                                 | Use when                                                   | Next server read                     |
62: | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
63: | [`updateTag(tag)`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag)                        | A Server Action must make its update visible immediately   | Waits for fresh data                 |
64: | [`revalidateTag(tag, 'max')`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag)         | The update is passive or stale data is acceptable          | Serves stale data while revalidating |
65: | [`revalidateTag(tag, { expire: 0 })`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) | A webhook or external system requires immediate expiration | Waits for fresh data                 |
66: 
67: ## Apply these patterns with SWR or TanStack Query
68: 
69: - [Client-side data fetching with SWR](/docs/app/guides/client-side-data-fetching/swr)
70: - [Client-side data fetching with TanStack Query](/docs/app/guides/client-side-data-fetching/tanstack-query)
71: 
72: See both patterns in the live [`next-spa-patterns` demo](https://next-spa-patterns.labs.vercel.dev) and its [source code](https://github.com/nextjs/next-spa-patterns).
```

Resolves with the completed run.\n *\n * A 400/500 response still carries a structured run body, so the caller can\n * render the typed failure; it is surfaced as a ConsolidationApiError with\n * that body attached.\n */\nexport async function startConsolidationRun(): Promise<ConsolidationRun> {\n  const response = await fetch(apiUrl(\"/api/consolidations/runs\"), {\n    method: \"POST\",\n    headers: { \"Content-Type\": \"application/json\" },\n    body: JSON.stringify({ period: \"FY2024\", scope: \"group\" }),\n    cache: \"no-store\",\n  });\n  const body = await parse<ConsolidationRun>(response);\n  if (!response.ok) {\n    throw new ConsolidationApiError(\n      body?.summary ?? `Consolidation run failed (HTTP ${response.status})`,\n      response.status,\n      body,\n    );\n  }\n  return body;\n}\n\n/** Fetch a previously executed run by id (the refresh path). */\nexport async function getConsolidationRun(\n  runId: string,\n): Promise<ConsolidationRun> {\n  const response = await fetch(\n    apiUrl(`/api/consolidations/runs/${encodeURIComponent(runId)}`),\n    { cache: \"no-store\" },\n  );\n  if (!response.ok) {\n    throw new ConsolidationApiError(\n      `Run ${runId} not found (HTTP ${response.status})`,\n      response.status,\n      null,\n    );\n  }\n  return parse<ConsolidationRun>(response);\n}\n\n/** Fetch the execution trace (events + tool calls) for a run. */\nexport async function getConsolidationTrace(\n  runId: string,\n): Promise<ConsolidationTrace> {\n  const response = await fetch(\n    apiUrl(`/api/consolidations/runs/${encodeURIComponent(runId)}/trace`),\n    { cache: \"no-store\" },\n  );\n  if (!response.ok) {\n    throw new ConsolidationApiError(\n      `Trace for run ${runId} not found (HTTP ${response.status})`,\n      response.status,\n      null,\n    );\n  }\n  return parse<ConsolidationTrace>(response);\n}\n",

1: ---
2: title: Building interactive apps
3: description: Learn how to build responsive interactions with Server Functions, transitions, optimistic UI, and pending feedback.
4: nav_title: Interactive apps
5: related:
6:   description: Learn more about the APIs used in this guide.
