13: 
14: When a user interaction requires server-side work, the result is not available immediately. Network requests take an unknown amount of time to complete and may succeed or fail. While waiting, the client should provide feedback and respond to those states. Otherwise, users are left looking at stale data and may wonder whether anything is happening.
15: 
16: This guide adds responsive feedback to a task management app called _Taskboard_. Each step handles a different kind of pending work, from streaming slow reads to confirming mutations before the server responds.
17: 
18: > **Good to know:** The patterns in this guide also improve [Core Web Vitals](https://web.dev/articles/vitals). Streaming with [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) lowers [FCP](https://web.dev/articles/fcp) and [LCP](https://web.dev/articles/lcp) by letting the shell paint while slow reads finish. Optimistic UI and transitions lower [INP](https://web.dev/articles/inp) by keeping the click frame fast. Prefetching the next route makes FCP, LCP, and INP on the destination page near-instant. These patterns help, but they don't replace the usual INP work: shipping less client JavaScript and avoiding blocking roundtrips during interactions.
19: 
20: ## Example
21: 
22: The patterns build in order: stream slow data behind loading boundaries, add an instant priority toggle, build a reusable filter with a callback prop, show comments before they're confirmed, move cards between columns on drop, manage form lifecycle in a create dialog, and signal pending deletion to a parent. The final step caches the reusable reads so navigations stay instant.
23: 
24: The companion [Taskboard demo](https://async-react-demo.labs.vercel.dev) ([source](https://github.com/nextjs/async-react-demo)) lets you see each pattern from this guide in action.
25: 
26: The app is organized by feature. Everything for the task domain (queries, Server Functions, and components) lives under `features/task/`. Shared UI primitives live in `components/ui/`, and pages in `app/` compose feature components. The file paths throughout this guide follow that structure.
27: 
28: The starting point is a Server Component app that reads tasks and comments from a database, with no [`<Suspense>`](/docs/app/guides/streaming) boundaries and no caching. Client Components call [Server Functions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) to mutate that data. After each mutation, the Server Function calls [`refresh()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/refresh) so the server re-renders with fresh data:
29: 
30: ```ts filename="features/task/task-actions.ts"
31: 'use server'
32: 
33: import { refresh } from 'next/cache'
34: import { PRIORITY_CYCLE } from '@/lib/data'
35: import { getTaskById, updateTaskPriority } from '@/lib/db'
36: 
37: export async function cyclePriority(taskId: string) {
38:   const task = await getTaskById(taskId)
39:   if (!task) return null
40:   const newPriority = PRIORITY_CYCLE[task.priority]
41:   await updateTaskPriority(taskId, newPriority)
42:   refresh()
43:   return newPriority
44: }
45: ```
46: 
47: ### Step 1: Stream slow data with Suspense
48: 
49: The task detail page reads the task and its comments. When both are awaited at the top of the page component, the whole page blocks until the slowest read resolves.
50: 
51: ```tsx filename="app/task/[id]/page.tsx"
52: import { getTask } from '@/features/task/task-queries'
53: import { TaskDetail } from '@/features/task/components/task-detail'
54: import { CommentSection } from '@/features/task/components/comment-section'
55: 
56: export default async function TaskPage({ params }) {
57:   const { id } = await params
58:   const task = await getTask(id)
59: 
60:   return (
61:     <div>
62:       <TaskDetail task={task} />
63:       <CommentSection taskId={id} />
64:     </div>
65:   )
66: }
67: ```
68: 
69: With this version, nothing renders until `getTask` resolves, and the comments read starts only after that.
70: 
71: Split the reads into separate components, pass each one a promise, and wrap them in [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense). The page becomes synchronous, returns the shell immediately, and the server streams each section in as its data resolves:
72: 
73: ```tsx filename="app/task/[id]/page.tsx"
74: import { Suspense } from 'react'
75: import {
76:   TaskDetail,
77:   TaskDetailSkeleton,
78: } from '@/features/task/components/task-detail'
79: import {
80:   CommentSection,
81:   CommentSectionSkeleton,
82: } from '@/features/task/components/comment-section'
83: 
84: export default function TaskPage({ params }) {
85:   return (
86:     <div>
87:       <Suspense fallback={<TaskDetailSkeleton />}>
88:         {params.then(({ id }) => (
89:           <>
90:             <TaskDetail id={id} />
91:             <Suspense fallback={<CommentSectionSkeleton />}>
92:               <CommentSection taskId={id} />
93:             </Suspense>
94:           </>
95:         ))}
96:       </Suspense>
97:     </div>
98:   )
99: }
100: ```
101: 
102: Each section component awaits its own data:
103: 
104: ```tsx filename="features/task/components/task-detail.tsx"
105: export async function TaskDetail({ id }) {
106:   const task = await getTask(id)
107:   return <TaskHeader task={task} />
108: }
109: ```
110: 
111: Calling `params.then()` inline in JSX keeps the page synchronous. The outer `<Suspense>` covers the params resolution and the task detail read. Once `TaskDetail` resolves, React reveals the task header and the nested `<Suspense>` boundary, which shows `CommentSectionSkeleton` while comments load.
112: 
113: The page shell now paints immediately, the task header streams in when `getTask` resolves, and the comments section follows when `getComments` resolves.
114: 
115: For more on streaming patterns, see the [Streaming](/docs/app/guides/streaming) guide.
116: 
117: ### Step 2: Respond instantly to a toggle
118: 
119: Each task card has a priority indicator that cycles through low, medium, and high on click.
120: 
121: The button renders the `priority` prop from the server. Calling a Server Function starts the mutation, but it doesn't change that prop in the current render.
122: 
123: Here the Server Function is called directly:
124: 
125: ```tsx filename="features/task/components/task-card.tsx"
126: 'use client'
127: 
128: import { cyclePriority } from '@/features/task/task-actions'
129: 
130: export function TaskCard({ id, priority }) {
131:   return (
132:     <button onClick={() => cyclePriority(id)} className={priorityDot[priority]}>
133:       {priority}
134:     </button>
135:   )
136: }
137: ```
138: 
139: If you click the dot, the Server Function runs, but the button keeps rendering the old `priority` prop until the next server render arrives.
140: 
141: Replace the direct call with [`useOptimistic`](https://react.dev/reference/react/useOptimistic) and [`useTransition`](https://react.dev/reference/react/useTransition). `useOptimistic` provides a value to render in place of the stale prop, and `useTransition` runs the Server Function as part of a transition. The optimistic value applies for as long as that transition is pending:
142: 
143: ```tsx filename="features/task/components/task-card.tsx"
144: 'use client'
145: 
146: import { useOptimistic, useTransition } from 'react'
147: import { cyclePriority } from '@/features/task/task-actions'
148: import { PRIORITY_CYCLE } from '@/lib/data'
149: 
150: export function TaskCard({ id, priority }) {
151:   const [optimisticPriority, setOptimisticPriority] = useOptimistic(priority)
152:   const [, startTransition] = useTransition()
153: 
154:   function handlePriority() {
155:     startTransition(async () => {
156:       setOptimisticPriority(PRIORITY_CYCLE[optimisticPriority])
157:       await cyclePriority(id)
158:     })
159:   }
160: 
161:   return (
162:     <button
163:       onClick={handlePriority}
164:       className={priorityDot[optimisticPriority]}
165:     >
166:       {optimisticPriority}
167:     </button>
168:   )
169: }
170: ```
171: 
172: The `setOptimisticPriority` call updates the UI on the current frame with the next value in the cycle. Reading from `optimisticPriority` instead of the prop means rapid double-clicks cycle correctly rather than reading a stale closure value.
173: 
174: When the transition ends and fresh data arrives, the optimistic value reverts to the new server-rendered prop. If the Server Function inside `useTransition` throws, the error is forwarded to the nearest [error boundary](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/error) without a manual `try`/`catch`.
175: 
176: The color now changes the moment the mouse lifts. Clicking again cycles to the next value without waiting for the first mutation to finish.
177: 
178: ### Step 3: Filter with pending feedback
179: 
180: The board has label filter chips (Design, Frontend, Backend). Clicking a chip updates a query param to filter the task list.
181: 
182: The selected filter comes from the URL. Calling `router.push()` starts a client navigation, and the server re-renders the board with the new search params. Until that navigation completes, the page keeps rendering the old URL state.
183: 
184: Here `router.push()` is called directly:
185: 
186: ```tsx filename="features/task/components/label-filter.tsx"
187: 'use client'
188: 
189: import { useRouter, useSearchParams } from 'next/navigation'
190: 
191: export function LabelFilter() {
192:   const router = useRouter()
193:   const searchParams = useSearchParams()
194: 
195:   function handleFilter(value: string | null) {
196:     const params = new URLSearchParams(searchParams.toString())
197:     if (value) params.set('label', value)
198:     else params.delete('label')
199:     router.push(`/?${params.toString()}`)
200:   }
201: 
202:   // ...render chips with onClick={handleFilter}
203: }
204: ```
205: 
206: With this version, `router.push()` starts the navigation, but there's no local pending state. The chip keeps rendering the old URL value, and the board gives no sign that a new server render is loading.
207: 
208: Separate the filter into two components. `LabelFilter` owns the query string update and passes the navigation callback to a reusable `ChipGroup`, which handles all the pending feedback:
209: 
210: ```tsx filename="features/task/components/label-filter.tsx"
211: 'use client'
212: 
213: import { useRouter, useSearchParams } from 'next/navigation'
214: import { ChipGroup } from '@/components/ui/chip-group'
215: 
216: const labels = [
217:   { label: 'Design', value: 'design' },
218:   { label: 'Frontend', value: 'frontend' },
219:   { label: 'Backend', value: 'backend' },
220: ]
221: 
222: export function LabelFilter() {
223:   const router = useRouter()
224:   const searchParams = useSearchParams()
225:   const current = searchParams.get('label') ?? null
226: 
227:   function filterAction(value: string | null) {
228:     const params = new URLSearchParams(searchParams.toString())
229:     if (value) {
230:       params.set('label', value)
231:     } else {
232:       params.delete('label')
233:     }
234:     router.push(`/?${params.toString()}`)
235:   }
236: 
237:   return (
238:     <ChipGroup items={labels} value={current} changeAction={filterAction} />
239:   )
240: }
241: ```
242: 
243: `LabelFilter` decides where the app navigates and holds no pending state of its own.
244: 
245: #### Handle pending feedback internally
246: 
247: `ChipGroup` accepts a `changeAction` prop and calls it inside its own `startTransition`. It uses two `useOptimistic` hooks: one for the selected chip, and one for the `data-pending` attribute that ancestor components can style against:
248: 
249: ```tsx filename="components/ui/chip-group.tsx"
250: 'use client'
251: 
252: import { startTransition, useOptimistic } from 'react'
253: 
254: export function ChipGroup({ items, value, changeAction }) {
255:   const [optimisticValue, setOptimisticValue] = useOptimistic(value)
256:   const [isPending, setIsPending] = useOptimistic(false)
257: 
258:   function handleClick(newValue) {
259:     startTransition(async () => {
260:       setOptimisticValue(newValue)
261:       setIsPending(true)
262:       await changeAction(newValue)
263:     })
264:   }
265: 
266:   return (
267:     <div className="flex gap-1.5" data-pending={isPending ? '' : undefined}>
268:       {items.map((item) => (
269:         <button
270:           key={item.value}
271:           onClick={() =>
272:             handleClick(item.value === optimisticValue ? null : item.value)
273:           }
274:           className={item.value === optimisticValue ? 'active' : ''}
275:         >
276:           {item.label}
277:         </button>
278:       ))}
279:     </div>
280:   )
281: }
282: ```
283: 
284: The consumer passes a callback (`changeAction`), and the design component runs it inside a transition. By convention, props named `action` or suffixed with `Action` signal this behavior. See [Exposing `action` props from components](https://react.dev/reference/react/useTransition#exposing-action-props-from-components) in the React docs for this pattern.
285: 
286: The `data-pending` attribute on the `ChipGroup` root element lets ancestor components react through CSS without any coordination. The board on the home page uses `group-has-data-pending:opacity-50` to dim while the transition runs, without replacing the board with a skeleton. Because `ChipGroup` renders inside the `group` element, the attribute is available to any ancestor for styling.
287: 
288: > **Good to know:** `group-has-data-pending:` and `has-data-pending:` compile to the CSS [`:has()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/:has) selector, which the browser re-evaluates over the anchored subtree whenever `data-pending` toggles. That stays cheap here because the board toggles it only twice per filter, and dragging (Step 5) deliberately skips it. Reach for client state instead when a broad `:has()` anchor toggles on a high-frequency interaction like dragging or scrolling, where repeated recalculation over a large subtree adds up.
289: 
290: The "Frontend" chip now highlights on the current frame. The board dims while the filtered data loads, then updates with the filtered tasks.
291: 
292: ### Step 4: Add comments with instant feedback
293: 
294: The task detail page has a comment section. Submitting a comment writes new data on the server, but a server component renders the persisted list, so it can't include the new comment until the next server render arrives.
295: 
296: Here a comment form uses controlled state for the input and calls the Server Function directly:
297: 
298: ```tsx filename="features/task/components/comment-form.tsx"
299: 'use client'
300: 
301: import { useState } from 'react'
302: import { addComment } from '@/features/task/task-actions'
303: 
304: export function CommentForm({ taskId }) {
305:   const [content, setContent] = useState('')
306: 
307:   async function handleSubmit() {
308:     if (!content.trim()) return
309:     await addComment(taskId, content)
310:     setContent('')
311:   }
312: 
313:   return (
314:     <div>
315:       <input
316:         value={content}
317:         onChange={(e) => setContent(e.target.value)}
318:         placeholder="Write a comment..."
319:       />
320:       <button onClick={handleSubmit}>Send</button>
321:     </div>
322:   )
323: }
324: ```
325: 
326: With this version, the Server Function runs on submit, but the input stays filled and the list doesn't change until the server responds.
327: 
328: Split the comment list into two parts. A server component renders the persisted comments, and a client component tracks only the **pending** comments using `useOptimistic([])` with an empty initial array. When the transition completes and a new render arrives with fresh data, the pending list resets to empty and the real comment appears in the server-rendered list:
329: 
330: ```tsx filename="features/task/components/optimistic-comments.tsx"
331: 'use client'
332: 
333: import { useOptimistic, useRef } from 'react'
334: import { addComment } from '@/features/task/task-actions'
335: import { CommentCard } from './comment-card'
336: 
337: export function OptimisticComments({ taskId }) {
338:   const [pendingComments, setPendingComments] = useOptimistic([])
339:   const formRef = useRef(null)
340: 
341:   return (
342:     <>
343:       <form
344:         ref={formRef}
345:         action={async (formData) => {
346:           const content = formData.get('content')?.trim()
347:           if (!content) return
348:           formRef.current?.reset()
349: 
350:           const id = crypto.randomUUID()
351:           setPendingComments((current) => [
352:             {
353:               id,
354:               content,
355:               userName: 'You',
356:               createdAt: new Date().toISOString(),
357:             },
358:             ...current,
359:           ])
360: 
361:           await addComment(taskId, content)
362:         }}
363:       >
364:         <input name="content" placeholder="Write a comment..." required />
365:         <button type="submit">Send</button>
366:       </form>
367:       {pendingComments.map((comment) => (
368:         <CommentCard key={comment.id} comment={comment} pending />
369:       ))}
370:     </>
371:   )
372: }
373: ```
374: 
375: Three things happen on submit:
376: 
377: 1. `formRef.current?.reset()` clears the input through direct DOM manipulation. Inside a transition, [`useState`](https://react.dev/reference/react/useState) setters are deferred until the transition completes, but `useOptimistic` setters and direct DOM calls like `formRef.reset()` apply on the current frame.
378: 2. `setPendingComments` adds the new comment to the pending list with a client-generated UUID.
379: 3. The form `action` runs the handler inside a transition.
380: 
381: The server component renders the real list alongside it:
382: 
383: ```tsx filename="features/task/components/comment-section.tsx"
384: import { getComments } from '@/features/task/task-queries'
385: import { CommentCard } from './comment-card'
386: import { OptimisticComments } from './optimistic-comments'
387: 
388: async function CommentSection({ taskId }) {
389:   const comments = await getComments(taskId)
390: 
391:   return (
392:     <div>
393:       <OptimisticComments taskId={taskId} />
394:       {comments.map((comment) => (
395:         <CommentCard key={comment.id} comment={comment} />
396:       ))}
397:     </div>
398:   )
399: }
400: ```
401: 
402: The input now clears on submit and a faded comment card appears at the top of the list. When the server confirms, the faded card disappears and the real comment takes its place in the server-rendered list.
403: 
404: ### Step 5: Move cards between columns
405: 
406: The board has three columns: Todo, In Progress, and Done. Each column renders tasks from the server-provided `tasks` prop.
407: 
408: Dropping a card starts a Server Function that writes the new status. The `tasks` prop doesn't change until the next server render arrives, so the client needs a temporary task list for the pending move.
409: 
410: Here the Server Function is called on drop:
411: 
412: ```tsx filename="features/task/components/board.tsx"
413: 'use client'
414: 
415: import { use } from 'react'
416: import { updateStatus } from '@/features/task/task-actions'
417: 
418: export function Board({ tasksPromise }) {
419:   const tasks = use(tasksPromise)
420: 
421:   function handleDrop(targetStatus, taskId) {
422:     updateStatus(taskId, targetStatus)
423:   }
424: 
425:   // ...render columns from tasks
426: }
427: ```
428: 
429: The component receives a promise from the parent server component (see Step 1's `<Suspense>` boundary) and unwraps it with [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use). With this version, a card dragged from "Todo" to "In Progress" stays in the old column while the server processes the update, then jumps to the new column after the response arrives.
430: 
431: Add `useOptimistic` with a reducer to remap the card's status on the current frame. The reducer receives the full task list and an action describing which card moved where:
432: 
433: ```tsx filename="features/task/components/board.tsx"
434: 'use client'
435: 
436: import { startTransition, use, useOptimistic } from 'react'
437: import { toast } from 'sonner'
438: import { updateStatus } from '@/features/task/task-actions'
439: 
440: export function Board({ tasksPromise }) {
441:   const tasks = use(tasksPromise)
442:   const [optimisticTasks, moveTask] = useOptimistic(
443:     tasks,
444:     (currentTasks, action: { taskId: string; status: Status }) =>
445:       currentTasks.map((t) =>
446:         t.id === action.taskId ? { ...t, status: action.status } : t
447:       )
448:   )
449: 
450:   function handleDrop(targetStatus, taskId) {
451:     startTransition(async () => {
452:       moveTask({ taskId, status: targetStatus })
453:       const result = await updateStatus(taskId, targetStatus)
454:       if (!result.success) toast.error(result.error)
455:     })
456:   }
457: 
458:   return (
459:     <div className="grid grid-cols-3 gap-4">
460:       {columns.map((col) => (
461:         <Column
462:           key={col.status}
463:           tasks={optimisticTasks.filter((t) => t.status === col.status)}
464:           onDrop={(taskId) => handleDrop(col.status, taskId)}
465:         />
466:       ))}
467:     </div>
468:   )
469: }
470: ```
471: 
472: The reducer maps over the task list and updates the status of the dragged card, leaving the rest unchanged. If a background refresh arrives mid-drag, for example from polling or another user's mutation, React re-runs the reducer with the updated base data so the optimistic move sits on top of fresh data. The Server Function returns an error result when the task no longer exists, which the client displays in a toast.
473: 
474: This step uses the standalone `startTransition` instead of `useTransition` because the hook's `isPending` would trigger the board fade from Step 3. The optimistic move already covers the visual feedback, so no pending indicator is needed. If the Server Function returns an expected error, the card reverts. Unexpected errors are forwarded to the nearest [error boundary](/docs/app/getting-started/error-handling).
475: 
476: A card dragged from "Todo" to "In Progress" now lands in the target column the moment you release.
477: 
478: ### Step 6: Manage form lifecycle
479: 
480: The board has a "New Task" button that opens a create dialog. The form action creates the task on the server, then refreshes the board.
481: 
482: The dialog coordinates three pieces of client state while the action is pending: the submit button, the field values, and whether the dialog is open. [`useActionState`](https://react.dev/reference/react/useActionState) handles all three.
483: 
484: Here a form manages submission state manually and calls the Server Function in an `onSubmit` handler:
485: 
486: ```tsx filename="features/task/components/create-task-modal.tsx"
487: 'use client'
488: 
489: import { useState } from 'react'
490: import { createTask } from '@/features/task/task-actions'
491: 
492: export function CreateTaskModal() {
493:   const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false)
494:   const [isSubmitting, setIsSubmitting] = useState(false)
495: 
496:   async function handleSubmit(e) {
497:     e.preventDefault()
498:     const formData = new FormData(e.currentTarget)
499:     const title = formData.get('title')
500:     if (!title.trim()) return
501: 
502:     setIsSubmitting(true)
503:     await createTask({ title /* ... */ })
504:     setIsSubmitting(false)
505:     setIsOpen(false)
506:   }
507: 
508:   return (
509:     <Dialog open={isOpen} onOpenChange={setIsOpen}>
510:       <form onSubmit={handleSubmit}>
511:         <input name="title" placeholder="Task title..." required />
512:         <button type="submit" disabled={isSubmitting}>
513:           {isSubmitting ? 'Creating...' : 'Create Task'}
514:         </button>
515:       </form>
516:     </Dialog>
517:   )
518: }
519: ```
520: 
521: With this version, the submit handler runs, but two separate `useState` calls manage the pending state. The dialog closes before the board shows the new task, because `setIsOpen(false)` fires outside of a transition. The form fields also keep their values across submissions unless you track a reset key yourself.
522: 
523: `useActionState` handles all three concerns: `isPending` for the button, key-based reset for the fields, and a wrap around the dialog close:
524: 
525: ```tsx filename="features/task/components/create-task-modal.tsx"
526: 'use client'
527: 
528: import { useActionState, startTransition, useState } from 'react'
529: import { createTask } from '@/features/task/task-actions'
530: 
531: export function CreateTaskModal() {
532:   const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false)
533: 
534:   const [{ key }, formAction, isPending] = useActionState(
535:     async (prev, formData) => {
536:       const title = String(formData.get('title'))
537:       if (!title.trim()) return prev
538: 
539:       await createTask({
540:         title,
541:         description: String(formData.get('description')),
542:         status: 'todo',
543:         priority: 'medium',
544:       })
545: 
546:       startTransition(() => setIsOpen(false))
547:       return { key: prev.key + 1 }
548:     },
549:     { key: 0 }
550:   )
551: 
552:   return (
553:     <Dialog open={isOpen} onOpenChange={setIsOpen}>
554:       <form action={formAction}>
555:         <div key={key}>
556:           <input name="title" placeholder="Task title..." required />
557:           <input name="description" placeholder="Describe the task..." />
558:         </div>
559:         <button type="submit" disabled={isPending}>
560:           {isPending ? 'Creating...' : 'Create Task'}
561:         </button>
562:       </form>
563:     </Dialog>
564:   )
565: }
566: ```
567: 
568: The `key` in the returned state controls form reset. On success, `key` increments, which remounts the `<div key={key}>` and resets every input inside it.
569: 
570: `useActionState` runs the action as a transition, so the dialog stays open and `isPending` stays `true` while `createTask` runs. State updates after the `await` aren't automatically part of that transition, so wrapping `setIsOpen(false)` in `startTransition` runs the close as part of the transition.
571: 
572: With that wrap in place, React batches the dialog close with the board update that `refresh()` triggers inside `createTask`, so the new task appears at the moment the dialog closes. Without it, the dialog closes first and the board updates a frame later.
573: 
574: > **Good to know:** This limitation is documented in React under [React doesn't treat my state update after `await` as a transition](https://react.dev/reference/react/useTransition#react-doesnt-treat-my-state-update-after-await-as-a-transition). Until it's fixed, wrapping post-`await` state updates in `startTransition` is the recommended workaround.
575: 
576: The same post-`await` window is where side effects like toasts belong:
577: 
578: ```tsx
579: await createTask({
580:   /* … */
581: })
582: 
583: startTransition(() => setIsOpen(false))
584: toast.success('Task created')
585: ```
586: 
587: Side effects that don't affect rendered state, such as analytics, toasts, and focus changes, run after the `await` resolves. They don't need a transition because they don't update React state.
588: 
589: The button text now changes to "Creating..." and dims on submit. When the server responds, the fields clear, the dialog closes, the new task appears on the board, and a toast confirms the action.
590: 
591: > **Good to know:** The companion app adds status, priority, assignee, and label pickers to the modal. The pattern is the same: hidden inputs track each picker's state, and `key` resets them all on success.
592: 
593: ### Step 7: Signal pending deletion to a parent
594: 
595: Each comment card has a delete button that removes the comment on the server, and the comment disappears from the list after the next render.
596: 
597: Between the click and that render, the card still shows the old data. The list itself can't show the pending removal, so the signal has to come from the button.
598: 
599: This step reuses the `data-pending` CSS hook from Step 3, but drives it from `useOptimistic(false)` instead of the `isPending` from `useTransition`.
600: 
601: Here the Server Function is called directly:
602: 
603: ```tsx filename="features/task/components/delete-button.tsx"
604: 'use client'
605: 
606: import { Trash2 } from 'lucide-react'
607: import { deleteComment } from '@/features/task/task-actions'
608: 
609: export function DeleteButton({ commentId }) {
610:   return (
611:     <button
612:       onClick={() => deleteComment(commentId)}
613:       aria-label="Delete comment"
614:     >
615:       <Trash2 className="size-3" />
616:     </button>
617:   )
618: }
619: ```
620: 
621: With this version, the comment stays fully visible until the next server render.
622: 
623: Wrap the action in a `<form>`, track pending state with `useOptimistic(false)`, and expose it through a `data-pending` attribute. Accept the action as a `deleteAction` prop so the parent comment card can react with CSS:
624: 
625: ```tsx filename="features/task/components/delete-button.tsx"
626: 'use client'
627: 
628: import { useOptimistic } from 'react'
629: import { Trash2 } from 'lucide-react'
630: 
631: export function DeleteButton({
632:   deleteAction,
633: }: {
634:   deleteAction: () => void | Promise<void>
635: }) {
636:   const [isPending, setIsPending] = useOptimistic(false)
637: 
638:   return (
639:     <form
640:       action={async () => {
641:         setIsPending(true)
642:         await deleteAction()
643:       }}
644:     >
645:       <button
646:         type="submit"
647:         disabled={isPending}
648:         data-pending={isPending ? '' : undefined}
649:         aria-label="Delete comment"
650:       >
651:         <Trash2 className="size-3" />
652:       </button>
653:     </form>
654:   )
655: }
656: ```
657: 
658: The parent comment card uses Tailwind's `has-data-pending:` variant to fade itself when any descendant sets the `data-pending` attribute. The button is the only component that knows when deletion is pending, so exposing that state as a CSS attribute lets any ancestor dim itself without lifting state or threading callbacks:
659: 
660: ```tsx filename="features/task/components/comment-card.tsx"
661: <div className="rounded-lg px-3 transition-all has-data-pending:opacity-30">
662:   {/* comment content */}
663:   {deleteAction && <DeleteButton deleteAction={deleteAction} />}
664: </div>
665: ```
666: 
667: The parent server component binds the Server Function to the comment ID, which keeps `DeleteButton` reusable:
668: 
669: ```tsx filename="features/task/components/comment-section.tsx"
670: <CommentCard
671:   comment={comment}
672:   deleteAction={
673:     comment.userName === 'You'
674:       ? deleteComment.bind(null, comment.id)
675:       : undefined
676:   }
677: />
678: ```
679: 
680: The card now fades to 30% opacity the moment the click registers. When the server confirms and the next render arrives, the card unmounts from the list.
681: 
682: ### Step 8: Make repeat navigation instant
683: 
684: Every pattern so far smooths a single interaction. Across navigations, the same reads rerun and the same fallbacks paint again. [Caching](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) the reusable reads and [prefetching](/docs/app/guides/prefetching) them with the real request closes that gap without moving the data model into the browser.
685: 
686: This step uses [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), introduced in Next.js 16. Steps 1 through 7 work without it. If you aren't using Cache Components, see [Caching without Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components).
687: 
688: Enable it in `next.config.ts`:
689: 
690: ```ts filename="next.config.ts"
691: import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
692: 
693: const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
694:   cacheComponents: true,
695: }
696: 
697: export default nextConfig
698: ```
699: 
700: Enabling Cache Components applies prerender validation across every route, not just the ones in this step. A route that reads request data such as `cookies()`, `headers()`, or `searchParams` outside [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) now blocks prerendering and needs the Step 1 treatment. To turn it on in an existing app, see [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components).
701: 
702: #### Cache reusable reads
703: 
704: For each server read, ask whether it should be reused across requests and whether each write can invalidate it precisely. A task is stable enough to cache and has a clear per-id tag:
705: 
706: ```ts filename="features/task/task-queries.ts"
707: import { cacheLife, cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
708: import { getTaskById } from '@/lib/db'
709: 
710: export async function getTask(id: string) {
711:   'use cache'
712:   cacheLife('hours')
713:   cacheTag('tasks', `task-${id}`)
714: 
715:   return getTaskById(id)
716: }
717: ```
718: 
719: The per-id tag `task-${id}` gives a single task its own handle. The broader `tasks` tag covers the list. See the [Caching guide](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) for cache scoping (`'use cache: private'`, `'use cache: remote'`), cache lifetimes, and tag patterns.
720: 
721: #### Invalidate from mutations
722: 
723: [`refresh()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/refresh) reruns dynamic work but leaves cached entries in place. Replace it with [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) for the tags each write touched:
724: 
725: ```ts filename="features/task/task-actions.ts"
726: 'use server'
727: 
728: import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
729: import { updateTaskStatus } from '@/lib/db'
730: 
731: export async function updateStatus(taskId: string, newStatus: Status) {
732:   const updated = await updateTaskStatus(taskId, newStatus)
733:   if (!updated) {
734:     return { success: false as const, error: 'Task no longer exists' }
735:   }
736: 
737:   updateTag('tasks')
738:   updateTag(`task-${taskId}`)
739:   return { success: true as const, status: newStatus }
740: }
741: ```
742: 
743: Every Server Function follows the same shape: run the write, then call `updateTag` for the cached reads that changed. Dynamic reads do not have tags to invalidate, so use `refresh()` for those mutations.
744: 
745: In this demo, the comment thread stays dynamic because readers expect the current discussion to update immediately on the open task page. Adding or deleting a comment calls `refresh()`, which reruns the dynamic comment read for the current route while leaving the task caches in place. See the [Revalidating guide](/docs/app/getting-started/revalidating) for tag patterns, time-based revalidation, and on-demand invalidation from route handlers.
746: 
747: #### Prefetch the destination with the real request
748: 
749: Under [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) (Next.js 16.3 and later), `<Link>` prefetches the destination's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): the route output that is shared across links for the current user. The shell does not include [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data), because `params` and `searchParams` are link-specific. Opt the link into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) with `prefetch={true}` to resolve that URL data ahead of the click:
750: 
751: ```tsx filename="features/task/components/task-card.tsx"
752: <Link href={`/task/${id}`} prefetch={true}>
753:   {/* … */}
754: </Link>
755: ```
756: 
757: Per-link prefetching is most valuable when the destination has URL-specific work that users are likely to need next. Cached reads make the prefetched output reusable and tag-invalidatable in the [Client Cache](/docs/app/glossary#client-cache); dynamic reads can still resolve before the click, but each prefetch can do real server work. In the companion app, the task cards prefetch the detail page as they scroll into view, so it paints instantly by the time the user clicks.
758: 
759: ## Next steps
760: 
761: The patterns in this guide combine a handful of primitives:
762: 
763: | Situation                                                                 | Use                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
764: | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
765: | Slow data should stream in without blocking the page                      | [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense)                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
766: | A value should update while async work runs                               | [`useOptimistic`](https://react.dev/reference/react/useOptimistic)                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
767: | Async work needs pending state, error handling, or coordinated UI updates | [`useTransition`](https://react.dev/reference/react/useTransition)                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
768: | A form needs pending, reset, and result state                             | [`useActionState`](https://react.dev/reference/react/useActionState)                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
769: | An ancestor should show pending state for work happening elsewhere        | [`data-pending`](https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/components/form#props) attribute styled with CSS                                                                                                                                                                      |
770: | Reusable reads should survive across requests and stay fresh after writes | [`'use cache'`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) with [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag), revalidated by [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) or [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) |
771: | Navigation between pages of an interactive app should feel instant        | [`<Link>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link) prefetching with [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching), and [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) via `prefetch={true}` for content that depends on URL data    |
772: 
773: Most patterns mix two or more of these. Reach for whichever primitive fits the constraint you're solving.
774: 
775: Related guides:
776: 
777: - [Client-side data fetching](/docs/app/guides/client-side-data-fetching) for direct browser fetching, providing initial data from a Server Component, and client cache coordination
778: - [Streaming](/docs/app/guides/streaming) for loading boundaries and `<Suspense>` patterns
779: - [Instant Navigation](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) for validating that navigations stay instant
780: - [View Transitions](/docs/app/guides/view-transitions) for animating state changes
781: - [Single-page applications](/docs/app/guides/single-page-applications#mutating-data-with-server-actions) for a shared-reducer `useOptimistic` example that keeps client and server list updates in sync

## Milestone complete — LedgerFlow API + UI Integration (Readiness Dashboard)

### 1. API endpoints implemented

New router `backend/app/api/consolidations.py`, registered in `create_app` (`backend/app/main.py`):

| Method | Path | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/api/consolidations/runs` | Starts a run via the **real `AgentRunner` → LangGraph → `ConsolidationSkill`**, persists it, returns the full result. `200` on success, `400` on invalid request, `500` on execution failure (typed body preserved). |
| `GET` | `/api/consolidations/runs/{run_id}` | Returns the persisted run (refresh path). `404` for unknown id. |
| `GET` | `/api/consolidations/runs/{run_id}/trace` | Returns persisted trace events + MCP tool calls. `404` for unknown id. |

Supporting artifacts:
- `backend/app/schemas/consolidation.py` — Pydantic request/response models (`extra="forbid"` on the request).
- `backend/app/services/consolidation_runs.py` — `ConsolidationRunStore` over the existing `storage/runs/` + atomic JSON write. No new persistence system.
- `create_app(mcp=None, runner_factory=None)` — a clean seam; production builds `AgentRunner(default_runtime(build_default_registry()))`, tests inject an in-memory-gateway runner. Execution is **synchronous** (no queue/background infra), which matches the existing architecture; the UI shows an explicit loading state.

### 2. Frontend pages/components created or modified
- **Created** `frontend/src/app/dashboard/consolidation/page.tsx` — page wrapper.
- **Created** `frontend/src/components/consolidation/consolidation-dashboard.tsx` — client dashboard with sections A–F: header (LedgerFlow, FY2024, GBP, run status), entity cards (US/USD, UK/GBP, IN/INR with real validation/mapping/balance data), Run Consolidation button (disabled + spinner while running), stage ledger (completed/blocked/pending/failed), issues panel (severity, code, description, source file/row, affected amount, treatment), and agent activity (trace events + MCP calls with status/duration).
- **Created** `frontend/src/lib/consolidation.ts` (typed API client over existing `apiUrl`) and `frontend/src/types/consolidation.ts`.
- **Modified** `frontend/src/lib/nav.ts` and `frontend/src/app/dashboard/page.tsx` — added a Consolidation nav item and module card.

### 3. Actual execution flow
`POST /api/consolidations/runs` → `create_app`'s runner factory → `AgentRunner.run(mode=CONSOLIDATION, payload={period, scope})` → LangGraph intent node selects the `consolidation` skill → `ConsolidationSkill` calls the read-only MCP tools through `ToolGateway` (loopback HTTP in prod, in-memory in tests) → result persisted → response. Live verification against a running server: **`list_entities` + 3× `get_trial_balance` + `get_fx_rates`**, all `ok`; 12 trace events from `execution_started` to `execution_completed`; status `blocked`; completed stages `trial_balance_ingestion`, `trial_balance_validation`, `account_mapping`; 7 blocked stages; entities US(25)/UK(23)/IN(20), all balanced, 0 unmapped; UK warning `group_account_name_mismatch`.

### 4. Persistence behavior
Filesystem only — one JSON file per run at `storage/runs/<run_id>.json` (gitignored). No PostgreSQL, no Gemini key. A run survives restart and is re-fetched by id; the UI writes the run id into the URL (`?run=...`) so a refresh reloads the persisted run.

### 5. Tests and results
- **Backend:** `backend/tests/test_consolidation_api.py` — 12 tests covering successful run, real runner→graph→skill execution, trace + issue propagation, no-Gemini path, refresh/persistence, unknown-run 404, invalid request 400/422, and execution-error 500 with preserved typed errors. **Full suite: 211 passed, 0 failed.** `compileall` clean.
- **Frontend:** `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint` clean on all new files, `next build` succeeds (`/dashboard/consolidation` prerendered).
- **Live E2E:** POST 200, GET 200, trace 200, invalid period 400, unknown run 404, extra field 422, no secret leakage in trace.

### 6. Exact scope respected
No new accounting calculations, no intercompany/FX/elimination logic, no Analysis skill or Copilot, no mock data as results, no `data/northwind/` changes (`git diff -- data/` empty), no staging or commits, no new agent/runner/registry/persistence systems — everything reuses the existing stack.

One operational note: the production MCP client targets `MCP_SERVER_URL` (default `http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp`), so run the backend on port 8000 (or set `MCP_SERVER_URL` to match) for consolidation runs to reach the tool server.

=== Docker compose config (frontend) ===
# LedgerFlow — Phase 1 infrastructure
#
# Three independent services:
#   frontend  -> http://localhost:3000  (Next.js)
#   backend   -> http://localhost:8000  (FastAPI)
#   db        -> localhost:5432         (PostgreSQL, intentionally unused)
#
# The backend has NO dependency on db: no connection string, no depends_on.
# The application works with `docker compose stop db`.

name: ledgerflow

services:
  frontend:
    build:
      context: ./frontend
      args:
        NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL: "http://localhost:${BACKEND_PORT:-8000}"
    image: ledgerflow-frontend
    container_name: ledgerflow-frontend
    ports:
      - "${FRONTEND_PORT:-3000}:3000"
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: production
      NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL: "http://localhost:${BACKEND_PORT:-8000}"
    healthcheck:
      test:
        [
          "CMD",
          "node",
          "-e",
          "fetch('http://127.0.0.1:3000').then((r) => process.exit(r.ok ? 0 : 1)).catch(() => process.exit(1))",
        ]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 30s
    networks:
      - ledgerflow
    restart: unless-stopped

  backend:
    build:
      context: ./backend
    image: ledgerflow-backend
    container_name: ledgerflow-backend
    ports:
      - "${BACKEND_PORT:-8000}:8000"
    environment:
      APP_ENV: ${APP_ENV:-development}
      SERVICE_NAME: ledgerflow-backend
      APP_VERSION: "0.1.0"
      CORS_ORIGINS: "http://localhost:${FRONTEND_PORT:-3000},http://127.0.0.1:${FRONTEND_PORT:-3000}"
      # Filesystem storage (no database configuration exists here by design).
      DATA_DIR: /app/data
      STORAGE_DIR: /app/storage
      OUTPUT_DIR: /app/output
      # LLM (optional): without a key the agent returns typed
      # llm_not_configured; add GEMINI_API_KEY to .env to enable it.
      GEMINI_API_KEY: <REDACTED>
      LLM_MODEL: ${LLM_MODEL:-}
      LLM_TEMPERATURE: ${LLM_TEMPERATURE:-0}
      # MCP: this app hosts the MCP server at /mcp and its agent connects
      # back to it over loopback inside the container.
      MCP_SERVER_URL: ${MCP_SERVER_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp}
      MCP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: ${MCP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS:-30}
      AGENT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS: ${AGENT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS:-25}
      AGENT_MAX_GRAPH_STEPS: ${AGENT_MAX_GRAPH_STEPS:-50}
    volumes:
      # Immutable source inputs
      - ./data:/app/data:ro
      # Writable persistence (runs, issues, agent logs) and report output
      - ./storage:/app/storage
      - ./output:/app/output
    healthcheck:
      test:
        [
          "CMD",
          "python",
          "-c",
          "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/health', timeout=3)",
        ]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 10s
    networks:
      - ledgerflow
    restart: unless-stopped
    # NOTE: intentionally no `depends_on: db` and no POSTGRES_* variables.

  db:
    # Official PostgreSQL image. Present as infrastructure for future use only;
    # nothing in the application connects to it during Phase 1.
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    container_name: ledgerflow-db
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB:-ledgerflow}
      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER:-ledgerflow}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: <REDACTED>
    volumes:
      - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U $${POSTGRES_USER} -d $${POSTGRES_DB}"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 10s
    networks:
      - ledgerflow
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  postgres_data:

networks:
  ledgerflow:
    driver: bridge
```

## 👤 User

# Milestone: Integrate LLM Reasoning into LedgerFlow Consolidation Agent

## Objective

Evolve LedgerFlow from its current deterministic consolidation-readiness workflow into a genuinely AI-powered, agentic financial consolidation system.

 LLM integration must be meaningful and visible in the actual execution workflow, not limited to a chatbot or a final report summarizer.

The LLM should understand accounting context, reason over source data, dynamically select tools, investigate discrepancies, propose accounting decisions, and coordinate workflow execution.

Python must remain the source of truth for financial calculations, validations, reconciliation verification, journal balancing, and financial statement figures.

**Core principle:**
- LLM = reasoning, interpretation, planning, investigation, recommendations and tool selection.
- Python = deterministic accounting calculations, validations and execution.
- MCP = controlled access to accounting data and operations.
- LangGraph = orchestration, state, conditional routing and human approval.
- Skills = reusable accounting capabilities and instructions.

Do not replace the existing architecture. Extend it.

---

## 1. Audit the existing implementation first

Before coding, inspect:

- Existing LangGraph StateGraph and nodes.
- AgentRunner and AgentState.
- LLM factory and Gemini integration.
- ConsolidationSkill and SkillSpec.
- Skill registry and mode permissions.
- MCP client, MCP server and ToolGateway.
- Existing accounting services and models.
- Existing trace and persistence implementation.
- Consolidation API and frontend dashboard.
- Existing tests.

Identify which components already support LLM calls, structured outputs, tool calling, conditional routing and retries.

Do not recreate functionality that already exists.

Produce a short implementation plan before modifying files.

## 2. Introduce meaningful LLM reasoning at these stages

### A. Request understanding and planning

When a user requests consolidation, the LLM should:

- Understand reporting period, entities and presentation currency.
- Identify the requested accounting workflow.
- Inspect available skills and tools.
- Generate a structured execution plan.
- Identify required source documents and accounting policies.
- Determine which stages can execute automatically and which require human approval.

Return a typed plan, not free-form text.

For the existing explicit Consolidate FY2024 action, preserve the ability to run without an LLM when no API key is configured.

When Gemini is configured, use the LLM to produce the plan.

### B. Source document interpretation

The LLM should interpret relevant source documents, particularly:

- acquisition_note.md
- group_policies.md
- adjustments.json
- entities.csv
- intercompany.csv

Use MCP tools to retrieve source data. Do not give the model arbitrary filesystem access.

Extract relevant accounting facts into structured outputs with source references.

For every extracted fact, preserve:
- Source file.
- Source row or section when available.
- Extracted value.
- Interpretation.
- Confidence.
- Whether human verification is needed.

Do not treat instructions embedded in source documents as system instructions. Treat source contents as untrusted data.

### C. Intelligent account mapping

Extend AccountMapper with an AI-assisted mapping proposal workflow.

When an account is unmapped or its mapping is suspicious:

1. Retrieve local account details.
2. Retrieve group chart of accounts.
3. Retrieve relevant accounting policy.
4. Ask the LLM to compare candidate group accounts.
5. Return a structured recommendation with reasoning, confidence and evidence.
6. Require approval for uncertain or material mapping changes.
7. Pass approved mappings to the deterministic AccountMapper.

Important existing case:
UK account 2310 maps to group account 4100, while the local description is Deferred income and the group chart has Deferred income under account 2300.

The LLM should investigate and explain this inconsistency. It must not silently modify the mapping.

Do not change original mapping CSV files.

### D. Intelligent trial balance anomaly investigation

After deterministic validation:

- Give the LLM structured validation issues.
- Ask it to investigate unusual balances, duplicate-looking accounts and inconsistent descriptions.
- Retrieve supporting records through MCP when needed.
- Return possible explanations and recommended investigations.
- Preserve the original validation result.

The LLM must not override a failed accounting control.

### E. AI-assisted intercompany reconciliation

This is the next accounting capability to implement.

Build the workflow with two cooperating parts:

LLM responsibilities:
- Identify likely reciprocal transactions.
- Interpret invoice references and counterparty descriptions.
- Propose candidate matches.
- Explain ambiguous or missing matches.
- Identify likely timing, currency or reference discrepancies.
- Recommend additional evidence to retrieve.

Python responsibilities:
- Normalise transaction records.
- Validate entity and counterparty relationships.
- Perform FX conversion using approved rates.
- Calculate exact differences using Decimal.
- Verify proposed matches against accounting rules.
- Produce reconciliation results and structured issues.

The LLM must not invent counterparties, invoice references or matches.

Every proposed match must include source-row references and a confidence score.

Never automatically accept an ambiguous match merely because the LLM has high confidence.

### F. FX translation

LLM responsibilities:
- Interpret the group's FX policy.
- Identify which rate types apply to each account category.
- Explain missing rates and unusual currency requirements.
- Recommend how an unresolved FX issue should be handled.

Python responsibilities:
- Resolve rates.
- Convert balances.
- Apply closing, average and historical rate policies.
- Calculate translation differences and reserves.
- Preserve precision using Decimal.

Use existing FXService. Do not duplicate FX logic.

### G. Elimination journal proposals

LLM responsibilities:
- Identify potential reciprocal intercompany balances and transactions.
- Determine which records appear eligible for elimination.
- Explain proposed elimination entries.
- Flag unmatched or ambiguous balances.

Python responsibilities:
- Verify eligibility.
- Generate debit/credit entries.
- Ensure journals balance.
- Check duplicate elimination.
- Preserve source traceability.

Journal proposals must be approved before posting if the accounting policy or evidence requires human review.

### H. Acquisition accounting, goodwill and NCI

LLM responsibilities:
- Interpret acquisition documents.
- Extract acquisition date, ownership percentage and relevant consideration.
- Identify missing inputs.
- Explain accounting assumptions and policy implications.

Python responsibilities:
- Calculate goodwill.
- Calculate NCI.
- Apply acquisition-date and post-acquisition profit rules.
- Produce attributable profit and closing equity calculations.

Existing case:
Northwind India was acquired on July 1, 2024, with 80% ownership.

Do not assume missing consideration, fair values or other acquisition inputs.

### I. Financial statement explanation

After deterministic statement assembly:

- Use the LLM to explain revenue and profit movements.
- Identify material changes between periods.
- Explain NCI and translation reserve movements.
- Explain unresolved issues and their possible impact.
- Generate management commentary with references to calculated figures.

Never allow the LLM to invent financial statement figures.

8: * ``copilot`` — intent is identified by the LLM (Gemini). An unkeyed
9:   environment produces the typed ``LLM_NOT_CONFIGURED`` error.
10: 
11: Flow::
12: 
13:     START -> load_context -> identify_intent -> select_skill
14:            -> execute_skill -> finalize -> END
15: 
16: Every node records trace events, and a failure at any step sets a typed
17: error in state and routes straight to ``finalize`` so the trace is always
18: completed. The LLM only orchestrates; skills call Python services for all
19: financial work.
20: """
21: 
22: from __future__ import annotations
23: 
24: import json
25: import re
26: from dataclasses import dataclass
27: from pathlib import Path
28: from typing import Any, Callable
29: 
30: from langchain_core.language_models.chat_models import BaseChatModel
31: from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage, HumanMessage, SystemMessage
32: from langgraph.graph import END, START, StateGraph
33: 
34: from app.agents.skills.base import SkillContext
35: from app.agents.skills.registry import SkillRegistry
36: from app.agents.state import (
37:     AgentError,
38:     AgentMode,
39:     AgentState,
40:     Intent,
41:     RunStatus,
42:     SkillResult,
43: )
44: from app.agents.thread_service import ThreadService
45: from app.agents.tracing import TraceRecorder
46: from app.core.config import Settings, settings as app_settings
47: from app.core.errors import (
48:     IntentIdentificationError,
49:     LedgerFlowError,
50:     LLMNotConfiguredError,
51:     SkillExecutionError,
52:     SkillNotFoundError,
53: )
54: 
55: # Provider that returns a chat model (or raises LLMNotConfiguredError).
56: LLMProvider = Callable[[], BaseChatModel]
57: 
58: 
59: @dataclass
60: class AgentRuntime:
61:     """Everything the shared graph needs, injected once.
62: 
63:     Keeping services on a runtime object (rather than globals) lets tests
64:     swap in a fake LLM, a temp storage dir and a test skill registry.
65:     """
66: 
67:     registry: SkillRegistry
68:     llm_provider: LLMProvider
69:     thread_service: ThreadService
70:     traces_dir: Path
71:     settings: Settings = app_settings
72:     tool_gateway: Any = None
73: 
74:     def optional_llm(self) -> BaseChatModel | None:
75:         """Return an LLM when configured, else None (never raises)."""
76:         try:
77:             return self.llm_provider()
78:         except LLMNotConfiguredError:
79:             return None
80: 
81:     def require_llm(self) -> BaseChatModel:
82:         """Return an LLM or raise the typed not-configured error."""
83:         return self.llm_provider()
84: 
85:     def trace(self, trace_id: str) -> TraceRecorder:
86:         return TraceRecorder(self.traces_dir, trace_id)
87: 
88: 
89: # --- intent helpers ---------------------------------------------------------
90: 
91: 
92: def _extract_json(text: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
93:     """Pull the first JSON object out of an LLM response."""
94:     cleaned = text.strip()
95:     fenced = re.search(r"```(?:json)?\s*(\{.*?\})\s*```", cleaned, re.DOTALL)
96:     if fenced:
97:         cleaned = fenced.group(1)
98:     start = cleaned.find("{")
99:     end = cleaned.rfind("}")
100:     if start == -1 or end <= start:
101:         return None
102:     try:
103:         parsed = json.loads(cleaned[start : end + 1])
104:     except json.JSONDecodeError:
105:         return None
106:     return parsed if isinstance(parsed, dict) else None
107: 
108: 
109: def _coerce_intent(data: dict[str, Any]) -> Intent:
110:     """Build a validated Intent from loosely typed LLM JSON."""
111:     def as_str(value: Any) -> str | None:
112:         if value is None:
113:             return None
114:         return str(value)
115: 
116:     raw_entities = data.get("entities") or []
117:     if isinstance(raw_entities, str):
118:         raw_entities = [raw_entities]
119:     entities = [str(e).strip() for e in raw_entities if str(e).strip()]
120: 
121:     try:
122:         confidence = float(data.get("confidence", 0.5))
123:     except (TypeError, ValueError):
124:         confidence = 0.5
125: 
126:     return Intent(
127:         kind=str(data.get("kind") or "financial_analysis"),
128:         topic=as_str(data.get("topic")),
129:         period=as_str(data.get("period")),
130:         scope=as_str(data.get("scope")),
131:         entities=entities,
132:         skill_hint=as_str(data.get("skill_hint")),
133:         requires_tools=bool(data.get("requires_tools", False)),
134:         confidence=max(0.0, min(1.0, confidence)),
135:         source="llm",
136:         user_goal=as_str(data.get("user_goal")) or as_str(data.get("question")),
137:     )
138: 
139: 
140: _PERIOD_RE = re.compile(r"\b(20\d{2})\b")
141: _ENTITY_RE = re.compile(r"\b(US|UK|IN)\b")
142: 
143: 
144: def heuristic_copilot_intent(user_input: str) -> Intent:
145:     """Keyword fallback when the LLM returns unusable intent JSON."""
146:     period_match = _PERIOD_RE.search(user_input)
147:     entities = sorted(set(_ENTITY_RE.findall(user_input)))
148:     lowered = user_input.lower()
149:     topic = "general"
150:     for keyword in ("revenue", "margin", "profit", "variance", "cash", "balance"):
151:         if keyword in lowered:
152:             topic = keyword
153:             break
154:     return Intent(
155:         kind="financial_analysis",
156:         topic=topic,
157:         period=period_match.group(1) if period_match else None,
158:         entities=entities,
159:         requires_tools=True,
160:         confidence=0.3,
161:         source="heuristic",
162:         user_goal=user_input,
163:     )
164: 
165: 
166: def consolidation_intent(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> Intent:
167:     """Deterministic intent for a consolidation run (no LLM involved)."""
168:     entities = payload.get("entities") or []
169:     if isinstance(entities, str):
170:         entities = [entities]
171:     return Intent(
172:         kind="consolidation",
173:         topic="consolidation_run",
174:         period=str(payload["period"]) if payload.get("period") else None,
175:         scope=str(payload.get("scope") or "group"),
176:         entities=[str(e) for e in entities],
177:         skill_hint=str(payload["skill"]) if payload.get("skill") else None,
178:         requires_tools=True,
179:         confidence=1.0,
180:         source="deterministic",
181:     )
182: 
183: 
184: COPILOT_INTENT_PROMPT = """\
185: You identify the financial intent of a user's question for LedgerFlow, a
186: multi-entity consolidation platform. Available skills:
187: {skills}
188: 
189: Respond with ONLY a JSON object (no prose, no code fences) matching:
190: {{"kind": "financial_analysis", "topic": string, "period": string|null,
191:   "scope": string|null, "entities": [string], "skill_hint": string|null,
192:   "requires_tools": boolean, "confidence": number between 0 and 1,
193:   "user_goal": string}}
194: 
195: Prior conversation turns (for context only):
196: {history}
197: 
198: User question:
199: {question}"""
200: 
201: 
202: # --- graph nodes ------------------------------------------------------------
203: 
204: 
205: def build_graph(runtime: AgentRuntime):  # noqa: C901 - node wiring is inherently linear
206:     """Compile the shared core agent graph bound to ``runtime``."""
207: 
208:     def _fail(
209:         state: AgentState, exc: LedgerFlowError, event: str
210:     ) -> dict[str, Any]:
211:         trace = runtime.trace(state["trace_id"])
212:         trace.event(event, exc.to_dict(), secrets=[_secret(runtime)])
213:         return {
214:             "status": RunStatus.FAILED,
215:             "errors": [AgentError(**exc.to_dict())],
216:             "summary": exc.message,
217:         }
218: 
219:     async def load_context(state: AgentState) -> dict[str, Any]:
220:         trace = runtime.trace(state["trace_id"])
221:         trace.event(
222:             "execution_started",
223:             {
224:                 "run_id": state["run_id"],
225:                 "mode": state["mode"].value,
226:                 "thread_id": state.get("thread_id"),
227:                 "skill": state.get("skill_name"),
228:             },
229:             secrets=[_secret(runtime)],
230:         )
231:         trace.event(
232:             "context_loaded",
233:             {"messages": len(state.get("messages", []))},
234:         )
235:         return {"status": RunStatus.RUNNING}
236: 
237:     async def identify_intent(state: AgentState) -> dict[str, Any]:
238:         trace = runtime.trace(state["trace_id"])
239:         mode = state["mode"]
240: 
241:         try:
242:             if mode is AgentMode.CONSOLIDATION:
243:                 intent = consolidation_intent(state.get("payload") or {})
244:                 if not intent.period:
245:                     raise IntentIdentificationError(
246:                         "consolidation requires a period",
247:                         details={"payload": sorted(state.get("payload") or {})},
248:                     )
249:             else:
250:                 llm = runtime.require_llm()
251:                 skills_json = json.dumps(
252:                     runtime.registry.describe(mode), indent=2
253:                 )
254:                 history = state.get("history") or []
255:                 history_text = (
256:                     json.dumps(history[-6:], indent=2) if history else "(none)"
257:                 )
258:                 question = state.get("user_input") or ""
259:                 response = await llm.ainvoke(
260:                     [
261:                         SystemMessage(
262:                             content=COPILOT_INTENT_PROMPT.format(
263:                                 skills=skills_json,
264:                                 history=history_text,
265:                                 question=question,
266:                             )
267:                         ),
268:                         HumanMessage(content=question),
269:                     ]
270:                 )
271:                 data = _extract_json(
272:                     response.content
273:                     if isinstance(response.content, str)
274:                     else str(response.content)
275:                 )
276:                 if data is None:
277:                     intent = heuristic_copilot_intent(question)
278:                     trace.event(
279:                         "intent_fallback",
280:                         {"reason": "unparseable_llm_response"},
281:                     )
282:                 else:
283:                     intent = _coerce_intent(data)
284:         except LedgerFlowError as exc:
285:             return _fail(state, exc, "intent_failed")
286:         except Exception as exc:  # provider/network failure
287:             from app.core.errors import LLMInvocationError
288: 
289:             return _fail(
290:                 state,
291:                 LLMInvocationError(
292:                     f"LLM intent identification failed: {exc}",
293:                     details={"mode": mode.value},
294:                 ),
295:                 "intent_failed",
296:             )
297: 
298:         trace.event(
299:             "intent_identified",
300:             {
301:                 "kind": intent.kind,
302:                 "source": intent.source,
303:                 "confidence": intent.confidence,
304:                 "period": intent.period,
305:                 "entities": intent.entities,
306:             },
307:         )
308:         return {"intent": intent}
309: 
310:     def route_after_intent(state: AgentState) -> str:
311:         if state.get("status") is RunStatus.FAILED or not state.get("intent"):
312:             return "finalize"
313:         return "select_skill"
314: 
315:     async def select_skill(state: AgentState) -> dict[str, Any]:
316:         trace = runtime.trace(state["trace_id"])
317:         intent: Intent = state["intent"]
318:         mode = state["mode"]
319:         try:
320:             skill = runtime.registry.select_by_intent(
321:                 intent.kind, mode, hint=intent.skill_hint
322:             )
323:             if skill is None:
324:                 available = [s.spec.name for s in runtime.registry.for_mode(mode)]
325:                 raise SkillNotFoundError(
326:                     f"no skill available for intent '{intent.kind}' in mode "
327:                     f"'{mode.value}'",
328:                     details={
329:                         "intent": intent.kind,
330:                         "mode": mode.value,
331:                         "available": available,
332:                     },
333:                 )
334:         except LedgerFlowError as exc:
335:             return _fail(state, exc, "skill_selection_failed")
336: 
337:         trace.event(
338:             "skill_selected",
339:             {
340:                 "skill": skill.name,
341:                 "mode": mode.value,
342:                 "hint": intent.skill_hint,
343:                 "has_instructions": skill.instructions_doc() is not None,
344:             },
345:         )
346:         return {"skill_name": skill.name}
347: 
348:     def route_after_skill(state: AgentState) -> str:
349:         if state.get("status") is RunStatus.FAILED or not state.get("skill_name"):
350:             return "finalize"
351:         return "execute_skill"
352: 
353:     async def execute_skill(state: AgentState) -> dict[str, Any]:
354:         trace = runtime.trace(state["trace_id"])
355:         bound_gateway: Any = None
356:         try:
357:             skill = runtime.registry.get(state["skill_name"])
358:             # The selected skill's own SKILL.md is made available to it here;
359:             # no other skill's instructions are exposed.
360:             instructions_doc = skill.instructions_doc()
361:             # Policy is bound to the skill's static spec + mode, never to
362:             # model output; the skill only ever sees this bound view.
363:             if runtime.tool_gateway is not None:
364:                 bound_gateway = runtime.tool_gateway.bind(
365:                     skill=skill.spec,
366:                     mode=state["mode"],
367:                     trace=trace,
368:                     secrets=[_secret(runtime)],
369:                 )
370:             context = SkillContext(
371:                 mode=state["mode"],
372:                 intent=state["intent"],
373:                 user_input=state.get("user_input"),
374:                 payload=state.get("payload") or {},
375:                 llm=runtime.optional_llm(),
376:                 trace=trace,
377:                 tool_gateway=bound_gateway,
378:                 settings=runtime.settings,
379:                 skill_instructions=instructions_doc,
380:             )
381:             trace.event("skill_started", {"skill": skill.name})
382:             result = await skill.execute(context)
383:         except LedgerFlowError as exc:
384:             return _with_records(
385:                 _fail(state, exc, "skill_execution_failed"), bound_gateway
386:             )
387:         except Exception as exc:
388:             return _with_records(
389:                 _fail(
390:                     state,
391:                     SkillExecutionError(
392:                         f"skill '{state.get('skill_name')}' raised: {exc}",
393:                         details={"skill": state.get("skill_name")},
394:                     ),
395:                     "skill_execution_failed",
396:                 ),
397:                 bound_gateway,
398:             )
399: 
400:         trace.event(
401:             "skill_executed",
402:             {
403:                 "skill": skill.name,
404:                 "status": result.status.value,
405:                 "tool_calls": len(result.tool_calls),
406:                 "issues": len(result.issues),
407:             },
408:         )
409:         # The gateway is the source of truth for MCP tool records; a skill
410:         # that re-surfaced them in its own result is de-duplicated here.
411:         records = list(result.tool_calls)
412:         if bound_gateway is not None:
413:             records.extend(
414:                 r for r in bound_gateway.records if r not in records
415:             )
416:         return {
417:             "skill_result": result,
418:             "tool_calls": records,
419:             "status": result.status,
420:         }
421: 
422:     async def finalize(state: AgentState) -> dict[str, Any]:
423:         trace = runtime.trace(state["trace_id"])
424:         result: SkillResult | None = state.get("skill_result")
425:         status = state.get("status", RunStatus.FAILED)
426: 
427:         if result is not None:
428:             status = result.status
429:             summary = result.summary
430:         else:
431:             summary = state.get("summary") or "execution failed"
432: 
433:         updates: dict[str, Any] = {"status": status, "summary": summary}
434: 
435:         # Only a successful execution produces an assistant turn; failures
436:         # surface through the API response, not a fabricated reply.
437:         if result is not None:
438:             answer = result.answer or summary
439:             updates["messages"] = [AIMessage(content=answer)]
440: 
441:         trace.event(
442:             "execution_completed",
443:             {
444:                 "status": status.value,
445:                 "summary": summary,
446:                 "skill": state.get("skill_name"),
447:                 "errors": [e.code for e in state.get("errors", [])],
448:             },
449:             secrets=[_secret(runtime)],
450:         )
451:         return updates
452: 
453:     builder = StateGraph(AgentState)
454:     builder.add_node("load_context", load_context)
455:     builder.add_node("identify_intent", identify_intent)
456:     builder.add_node("select_skill", select_skill)
457:     builder.add_node("execute_skill", execute_skill)
458:     builder.add_node("finalize", finalize)
459: 
460:     builder.add_edge(START, "load_context")
461:     builder.add_edge("load_context", "identify_intent")
462:     builder.add_conditional_edges(
463:         "identify_intent",
464:         route_after_intent,
465:         {"select_skill": "select_skill", "finalize": "finalize"},
466:     )
467:     builder.add_conditional_edges(
468:         "select_skill",
469:         route_after_skill,
470:         {"execute_skill": "execute_skill", "finalize": "finalize"},
471:     )
472:     builder.add_edge("execute_skill", "finalize")
473:     builder.add_edge("finalize", END)
474:     return builder.compile()
475: 
476: 
477: def _secret(runtime: AgentRuntime) -> str:
478:     """The API key to scrub from any trace payload."""
479:     return runtime.settings.gemini_api_key or ""
480: 
481: 
482: def _with_records(
483:     update: dict[str, Any], bound_gateway: Any
484: ) -> dict[str, Any]:
485:     """Surface gateway tool records even when the skill failed mid-call."""
486:     if bound_gateway is not None and bound_gateway.records:
487:         update["tool_calls"] = list(bound_gateway.records)
488:     return update
489: 
490: 
491: def default_runtime(registry: SkillRegistry | None = None) -> AgentRuntime:
492:     """Runtime wired to process settings and filesystem storage.
493: 
494:     The tool gateway connects to the MCP server mounted on this same
495:     FastAPI process (loopback), with per-call sessions and a cached
496:     tool catalogue. Skills reach tools only through this gateway, which
497:     enforces their static ``permitted_tools`` and ``ToolPolicy``.
498:     """
499:     from app.agents.llm import create_chat_model
500:     from app.mcp.client import MCPClient
501:     from app.mcp.gateway import ToolGateway
502:     from app.storage.filesystem import storage_paths
503: 
504:     storage_paths.ensure_layout()
505:     return AgentRuntime(
506:         registry=registry or SkillRegistry(),
507:         llm_provider=lambda: create_chat_model(app_settings),
508:         thread_service=ThreadService(storage_paths.threads_dir),
509:         traces_dir=storage_paths.traces_dir,
510:         settings=app_settings,
511:         tool_gateway=ToolGateway(
512:             MCPClient(app_settings.mcp_server_url), settings=app_settings
513:         ),
514:     )

18: # Keys whose values are always masked, regardless of content.
19: _SENSITIVE_KEY_RE = re.compile(
20:     r"(api[_-]?key|authorization|bearer|password|secret|token|credential)",
21:     re.IGNORECASE,
22: )
23: 
24: # Values that look like common API key formats.

28: ]

30: _MASK = "***REDACTED***"
31: 
32: 
33: def redact(value: Any, extra_secrets: Iterable[str] = ()) -> Any:
34:     """Recursively mask secrets in strings, dicts and lists."""
35:     secrets = [s for s in extra_secrets if s and len(s) >= 8]
36: 
37:     if isinstance(value, str):
38:         out = value
39:         for secret in secrets:
40:             if secret in out:
41:                 out = out.replace(secret, _MASK)
42:         for pattern in _SENSITIVE_VALUE_RES:
43:             out = pattern.sub(_MASK, out)
44:         return out
45:     if isinstance(value, dict):
46:         redacted: dict[Any, Any] = {}
47:         for key, item in value.items():
48:             if isinstance(key, str) and _SENSITIVE_KEY_RE.search(key):
49:                 redacted[key] = _MASK
50:             else:
51:                 redacted[key] = redact(item, secrets)
52:         return redacted
53:     if isinstance(value, list):
54:         return [redact(item, secrets) for item in value]
55:     if isinstance(value, tuple):

64: class TraceRecorder:

67:     def __init__(self, traces_dir: str | Path, trace_id: str) -> None:
68:         self.trace_id = trace_id

70:         # Resume numbering so a recorder rebuilt for the same trace (one is
71:         # created per graph node) continues the file instead of restarting.
72:         self._seq = 0
73:         if self.path.is_file():
74:             try:
75:                 with self.path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
76:                     self._seq = sum(1 for line in handle if line.strip())
77:             except OSError:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
78:                 self._seq = 0

87:         """Append one event; returns the record that was written."""
88:         self._seq += 1
89:         record = {
90:             "ts": _now(),
91:             "seq": self._seq,
92:             "trace_id": self.trace_id,
93:             "event": event,
94:             "payload": redact(payload or {}, secrets),

96:         append_jsonl(self.path, record)
97:         return record

103:         return list(iter_jsonl(self.path))
